evidence.claim: The 2022 report says Pakistan faced serious human rights issues including arbitrary killings, enforced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on expression and assembly, and widespread impunity for abuses.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 report says Pakistan faced serious human rights issues including arbitrary killings, enforced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on expression and assembly, and widespread impunity for abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government human-rights report summarizing the year's record with detailed attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the exact 2022 period, including the Sharif-led government from April onward.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the Sharif government, though some problems predated him and security agencies retained substantial autonomy.
contrary_evidence: The same summary notes a constitutional parliamentary transition to Sharif rather than an immediate breakdown of formal civilian institutions.

evidence.claim: HRW says violence against women and girls remained widespread, the government did little to stop child and forced marriage, and at least seven transgender women were killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2022 while minority communities remained vulnerable to abuse.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: HRW says violence against women and girls remained widespread, the government did little to stop child and forced marriage, and at least seven transgender women were killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2022 while minority communities remained vulnerable to abuse.
evidence.source_locator: women and girls plus gender-identity sections, lines 92-98 and 114-115
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights reporting with concrete 2022 findings and multiple vulnerable-group categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited social and legal conditions, but the Sharif government is relevant for failure to protect and remediate.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes one positive institutional step in January 2022, the workplace-harassment amendment, which shows the picture was not uniformly negative.

evidence.claim: After the Islamabad High Court said successive chief executives had given tacit approval to enforced disappearances, the federal government formed a seven-member committee under the law minister to deliberate policy, and the PM was briefed on the issue.
evidence.title: Govt forms committee to 'deliberate policy' on enforced disappearances
evidence.excerpt: After the Islamabad High Court said successive chief executives had given tacit approval to enforced disappearances, the federal government formed a seven-member committee under the law minister to deliberate policy, and the PM was briefed on the issue.
evidence.source_locator: Dawn summary of the IHC order and ministry notification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a formal government notification and court order; direct PM-level ordering is still indirect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows Sharif's government responding after judicial notice; it does not prove he personally designed the disappearance policy.
contrary_evidence: The underlying practice predates Sharif and the operational actors are not named here.

evidence.claim: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
evidence.title: NCHR Statement on IHC Ruling on Enforced Disappearances
evidence.publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statutory human-rights body summarizing the court ruling and government response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for attribution of Sharif's government as the addressed authority; weak for proving personal operational direction.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not identify which security actors carried out individual disappearances.

evidence.claim: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Braving the Storm: Enforced disappearances and the right to protest in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report with a clear 2022 scope and specific abuse pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports a state-abuse pattern under Sharif's term, but it does not by itself prove his personal ordering of each incident.
contrary_evidence: The report attributes the abuses to state forces generally, not to Sharif personally.

evidence.claim: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
evidence.title: IHC orders inquiry into claims of torture on Gill
evidence.excerpt: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
evidence.source_locator: report of the IHC order and the court's directions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Court order summarized by a mainstream local outlet; the underlying court record is the stronger source but was not directly accessible here.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly implicates the police custody chain during Sharif's government, but not a proven personal order by Sharif.
contrary_evidence: Police and government officials denied torture; the dispute remained under inquiry.

evidence.claim: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
evidence.title: Press Release: NCHR Inquiry Report on Custodial Torture at Central Jail (Adiala), Rawalpindi
evidence.publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs describing the inquiry findings and court directions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official inquiry report announcement with concrete findings and a court-ordered response chain.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for prison administration under the federal government; still indirect for naming Sharif as the actor behind abuse.
contrary_evidence: The report describes jail conditions and responsible public servants, not a personal PM order.

evidence.claim: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
evidence.title: Alvi concerned over treatment of journalists
evidence.excerpt: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
evidence.source_locator: Dawn summary of the president's letter
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct written notice to Sharif from the head of state.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is direct notice to Sharif and his government; it still does not prove he personally directed the harassment.
contrary_evidence: The letter is a warning and request, not proof of authorial control over every abuse.

evidence.claim: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
evidence.title: NCHR launches complaint cell for women journalists
evidence.excerpt: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
evidence.source_locator: article body describing the launch and the consultative meeting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of an official human-rights initiative with specific abuse descriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Useful as evidence of a documented abuse environment and institutional response; the PM link remains indirect unless paired with the president's letter.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish direct PM-level authorship of the abuse campaigns.

evidence.claim: NCHR's minority report said nearly half of reserved minority posts were vacant, 80% of non-Muslims in filled posts were in BPS 01-04, and the Ministry of Human Rights sent letters to provincial chief secretaries directing them to protect minority rights.
evidence.title: NCHR launches fact finding report on minority rights

judge.chapter_rationale: Pakistan under Shehbaz Sharif is a serious but not fully collapsed domestic-safety case. At the same time, Sharif's government did enact a torture-and-custodial-death bill and moved, under judicial pressure, toward committees and inquiries on disappearances and custody abuse. Those remedies are real and matter, but they are not yet enough to transform the safety environment. judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Shehbaz Sharif's record on domestic safety in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The 2022 report says Pakistan faced serious human rights issues including arbitrary killings, enforced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on expression and assembly, and widespread impunity for abuses; and Specific torture allegations after high-profile arrests show coercive policing and detention practice.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Media pressure and blocking continued through 2022, which weakens any claim of a safe civic space; and Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed: direct for some legislative and committee choices, indirect for many security-service abuses and custody conditions.

Taken together, I did not go higher because I rejected 5+ because the evidence still shows serious custody abuse, media pressure, and unresolved disappearances. I did not go lower because I rejected 2-3 because the file contains meaningful legal and inquiry responses, so it is not a pure repression record.

evidence.claim: Reuters said parliament chose Shehbaz Sharif after a no-confidence vote in a week-long constitutional confrontation, and that the nuclear-armed country was likely to remain prone to political and economic turbulence.
evidence.title: Pakistan parliament elects Sharif PM as Khan MPs quit en masse
evidence.excerpt: Reuters said parliament chose Shehbaz Sharif after a no-confidence vote in a week-long constitutional confrontation, and that the nuclear-armed country was likely to remain prone to political and economic turbulence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting, but the article is a short political summary rather than a nuclear-policy document.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context for inherited constraints, not proof of nuclear conduct.
contrary_evidence: This is broad political context, not direct evidence of nuclear decision-making.

evidence.claim: The federal government instructed PEMRA to lift the ban on broadcasting Imran Khan's speech, and the information minister said the prime minister had directed PEMRA to implement Article 19 of the constitution.
evidence.title: Federal govt issues instructions to PEMRA for lifting ban on broadcasting Imran's speech
evidence.excerpt: The federal government instructed PEMRA to lift the ban on broadcasting Imran Khan's speech, and the information minister said the prime minister had directed PEMRA to implement Article 19 of the constitution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of an official instruction from the prime minister, with clear date and named implementing agency.
evidence.period_fit: Direct November 2022 action inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Sharif through the minister's statement; this is a concrete pro-opposition speech decision, though it followed earlier restrictions.
contrary_evidence: The action came after earlier broadcast restrictions, so it is partial and late rather than a clean baseline reform.

evidence.claim: Sharif strongly condemned the armed intrusion into anchor Shifa Yousafzai's home, asked the Islamabad IG for a report, and directed that the suspects be found and punished under the law.
evidence.title: شفا یوسفزئی کے گھر مسلح افراد کا دھاوا، وزیر اعظم نے واقعے کی رپورٹ طلب کرلی

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language outlet quoting the prime minister and police response; strong for the immediate response, weaker for any broader systemic conclusion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM response to an attack on a journalist; it shows a protective reaction to one incident, not durable system-wide protection.
contrary_evidence: The underlying incident shows journalists still faced severe insecurity.
A response to one attack does not prove sustained protection of the press.

evidence.claim: The Federal Investigation Agency detained eight people after they published criticism of the state on Twitter, and Amnesty said the arrests were part of a repressive crackdown on free expression online.

evidence.period_fit: Direct April 2022 conduct inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrests were carried out by FIA under the federal state; direct Sharif ordering is not established, but the pattern persisted under his government.
contrary_evidence: The source does not prove Sharif personally ordered the arrests.

evidence.claim: Families of the disappeared and activists who protest peacefully are sometimes met with violence by the state, intimidation, and arbitrary detention or arrest for exercising peaceful assembly.

evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 reporting on protest and disappearance-related abuse.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is state-level attribution rather than a single Sharif order; it captures the domestic safety climate under his government but much of the problem predates him.
contrary_evidence: Some of the underlying disappearance problem predates Sharif and is not uniquely attributable to him.

evidence.claim: Pakistani police fired teargas, baton-charged, and detained supporters of ousted PM Imran Khan to stop them reaching Islamabad to demand fresh elections.

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with concrete incident details and witnesses; attribution to national-level command is indirect, but the protest suppression itself is well documented.
evidence.period_fit: Direct May 2022 protest suppression inside the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The action was carried out by police and other authorities during the Sharif era; direct PM ordering is not shown, so attribution is institutional rather than personal.
contrary_evidence: Authorities justified the response as keeping order around an unannounced road blockade.
Direct Sharif instruction is not established in the report.

evidence.claim: RSF said it had registered nine cases of intimidation of Pakistani journalists by army-related agencies since Shehbaz Sharif became prime minister and warned the harassment was undermining democracy.
evidence.title: Behind Pakistan’s civilian government, army tightens its grip on journalists
evidence.excerpt: RSF said it had registered nine cases of intimidation of Pakistani journalists by army-related agencies since Shehbaz Sharif became prime minister and warned the harassment was undermining democracy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated advocacy report with named cases and explicit attribution; strong on the pattern, though the military-centric attribution limits direct PM culpability.
evidence.period_fit: Mid-2022, squarely within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: RSF links the harassment mainly to army-related agencies, which limits direct attribution to Sharif but still places the pattern under his watch.
contrary_evidence: RSF itself says the military was acting behind the scenes, so this is not a clean civilian-only responsibility case.

evidence.claim: ARY News was taken off the air in most major Pakistani cities and its news director was arrested; RSF said the civilian government was responsible for the latest attacks on the media while the military intervened behind the scenes.
evidence.title: Pakistani TV news channel taken off the air, news director arrested

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific dated incident with direct reporting and explicit attribution commentary, though the source itself notes behind-the-scenes military involvement.
evidence.period_fit: August 2022 action in the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report holds the current civilian government responsible for the latest attack while also pointing to military influence, so attribution is shared and incomplete rather than purely personal to Sharif.
contrary_evidence: The source says the military high command stamped the censorship, limiting direct attribution to the civilian prime minister.
The same report emphasizes recurring pressure across alternating governments.

evidence.claim: HRW said Pakistani authorities harassed and prosecuted human rights defenders and journalists for criticizing government policies, used blasphemy accusations and sedition laws against opponents and journalists, and failed to protect minorities and other at-risk groups in 2022.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Rights Besieged Amid Political Turmoil
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Pakistani authorities harassed and prosecuted human rights defenders and journalists for criticizing government policies, used blasphemy accusations and sedition laws against opponents and journalists, and failed to protect minorities and other at-risk groups in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: A retrospective annual report with concrete 2022 incidents and multiple corroborating themes; strong synthesis though it attributes broadly to authorities rather than a single decision-maker.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective but directly about 2022 conduct under the Sharif government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to Pakistani authorities during 2022, including the Sharif government, but the report does not isolate direct prime-ministerial commands.
contrary_evidence: This is a broad retrospective and not proof of a single Sharif order for each incident.
Some abuses predate Sharif and are institutional rather than personal.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The lifting of the broadcast ban on Imran Khan's speech is a concrete pro-speech move under Sharif's government.
Sharif's condemnation of the attack on Shifa Yousafzai and instruction to punish suspects shows a direct protective response to press intimidation.
The accession context confirms that Sharif entered office in a constitutional transition rather than a coup or closed succession.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The FIA's arrests over critical tweets are strong evidence of continued repression of online dissent.
Amnesty's account of violence and arbitrary detention against protesters and families of the disappeared shows a coercive civic environment.
Police tear-gassing and detaining supporters of the ousted PM while blocking their march to Islamabad is direct protest suppression.
RSF's reporting on intimidation by army-related agencies shows that coercive pressure on journalists persisted under Sharif.
The ARY off-air episode and arrest of its news director show serious media coercion and the limits of civilian control.
HRW's annual report on harassment and prosecutions of critics confirms the broader 2022 repression pattern.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Pakistan in 2022 was a fragile parliamentary system with strong military influence and extensive legacy restrictions on speech and protest. Sharif inherited a highly constrained environment and operated within a state where civilian authority remained incomplete.
judge.ruler_attribution: Mixed and often indirect: some actions are directly attributed to Sharif, but many coercive incidents are carried out by police, the FIA, or army-related agencies rather than by him personally.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The lifted broadcast ban is a real positive and prevents the score from falling lower.

judge.source_mix: A mix of official State House statements and Reuters plus Amnesty, RSF, and HRW. The strongest positive evidence is direct PM rhetoric; the strongest negative evidence is rights-monitor reporting on coercion by police, FIA, and army-linked agencies.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment; the judge relied entirely on the embedded projection and its cited evidence.
judge.chapter_rationale: Shehbaz Sharif's 2022 Pakistan is a constrained, mixed case. He made some clear pro-speech and pro-transfer statements, lifted one broadcast ban, and publicly instructed the military to stay apolitical. But the record is dominated by arrests over critical tweets, protest suppression, journalist intimidation, and media coercion by state and army-linked agencies. That is not a fully closed system, but it is far from a robustly free one. The score sits in the lower-middle range because Sharif displayed some restraint while presiding over a security state that continued to narrow political freedom.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the real, if limited, pro-speech and anti-third-term signals that separate Sharif from the hardest authoritarian cases.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would ignore the persistent coercion by the FIA, police, and army-related agencies that meaningfully constrained dissent and media freedom.

chapter_specific.value: Mixed and constrained: some civilian-restraint signals existed, but coercive institutions still dominated the civic space.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Shehbaz Sharif's record on political freedom in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The federal government instructed PEMRA to lift the ban on broadcasting Imran Khan's speech, and the information minister said the prime minister had directed PEMRA to implement Article 19 of the constitution; and Sharif strongly condemned the armed intrusion into anchor Shifa Yousafzai's home, asked the Islamabad IG for a report, and directed that the suspects be found and punished under the law.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: The Federal Investigation Agency detained eight people after they published criticism of the state on Twitter, and Amnesty said the arrests were part of a repressive crackdown on free expression online; and Families of the disappeared and activists who protest peacefully are sometimes met with violence by the state, intimidation, and arbitrary detention or arrest for exercising peaceful assembly.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed and often indirect: some actions are directly attributed to Sharif, but many coercive incidents are carried out by police, the FIA, or army-related agencies rather than by him personally.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would ignore the persistent coercion by the FIA, police, and army-related agencies that meaningfully constrained dissent and media freedom. I did not go lower because a lower score would miss the real, if limited, pro-speech and anti-third-term signals that separate Sharif from the hardest authoritarian cases.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Targeted subsidy relief was directed at lower-income households.

A career central banker was appointed to the State Bank, which supported stabilization.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Pakistan in 2022 was already in a serious balance-of-payments and inflation crisis when Sharif took office. The chapter therefore rewards stabilization work only if it is visible and credible against that inherited emergency.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The macro crisis remained severe despite the policy pivot.

judge.chapter_rationale: Sharif scores 3.5 because the dossier shows genuine stabilization intent and some competent administrative moves, but the crisis was still overwhelming by year end. Targeted relief, IMF progress, and a technocratic central-bank appointment are real positives; however, high inflation, reserve stress, and a balance-of-payments crisis kept the prosperity picture weak. This is a constrained crisis-management record with limited success, not a broad economic turnaround.

Inherited macro collapse, IMF conditionality, and external price shocks severely limited the government's room to improve outcomes quickly.
Relief was targeted, but household purchasing power remained badly strained and broad welfare gains were not yet visible.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Shehbaz Sharif's record on economic well-being in 2022 was assessed as poor, resulting in a score of 3.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: On the prime minister's directions, the finance minister pursued targeted subsidy proposals to provide immediate relief to lower-income households under a PM relief package; and The IMF said the FY2023 budget aimed for an underlying primary surplus of 0.4 percent of GDP, backed by current-spending restraint, higher-income tax mobilization, protected development spending, and a market-determined exchange rate, while expanding social safety and reforming SOEs.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Ishaq Dar took oath as finance minister while Pakistan was facing a balance-of-payments crisis, foreign reserves near one month of imports, a tumbling rupee, and inflation above 27 percent; and Pakistan's annual inflation was still 23.8 percent in November after 26.6 percent in October, showing that price pressures remained severe despite policy tightening.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Attribution is moderate: Sharif clearly made personnel, fiscal, and subsidy choices, but the crisis itself was inherited and IMF conditionality constrained his room for maneuver.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score near 4.5 would overstate the degree to which the crisis had been brought under control by 2022. I did not go lower because a score near 2.5 would understate the seriousness of the stabilization effort and the policy adjustments actually made.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Pakistan in 2022 faced one of the worst flood disasters in decades on top of fiscal stress and weak service coverage. That baseline means emergency relief deserves credit, but the score cannot move very high because the year is dominated by damage and recovery still underway.
judge.ruler_attribution: Sharif is directly tied to the relief and recovery decisions, but implementation depended heavily on BISP, NDMA, provinces, and external partners. The dossier supports real prime-ministerial responsibility, mostly in crisis response.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The floods themselves pushed millions into poverty, limiting what the response could accomplish.
Education disruption remained severe even after relief and temporary learning centers.

judge.source_mix: Official Pakistani government releases combined with UNDP, WFP, UNICEF, and World Bank documentation. The dossier is strongest on emergency response and weaker on durable post-disaster outcomes.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment, so the judgment relies on the embedded dossier evidence, the reviewer exclusions already present there, and cross-case calibration within the batch.
judge.chapter_rationale: Sharif gets a middle score because the dossier shows serious emergency welfare action after catastrophic floods: direct cash relief, expanded social protection, a recovery framework, and partner-supported reconstruction financing. The score is not higher because the disaster itself inflicted massive welfare losses and the record does not yet show completed recovery. This is a competent crisis-response year, not a full human-development turnaround.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the scale and speed of the flood-relief response and the direct prime-ministerial instructions behind it.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require evidence that the recovery framework had already translated into broad, durable improvements for flood-affected households by year-end.

flood-affected families, mothers, children, and vulnerable households are explicitly targeted

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Shehbaz Sharif's record on social well-being in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The prime minister directed that every flood-affected family receive Rs. 50,000 within three days, with BISP cash relief delivered under NDMA supervision and via electronic transfer so deserving people would get relief; and BISP said the federal government increased the flood-relief cash package from Rs. 28 billion to Rs. 70 billion and was distributing Rs. 25,000 per family transparently, including in Gilgit-Baltistan.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Floods pushed millions into poverty and destroyed housing, overwhelming the welfare environment; and UNICEF said more than 2 million children remained out of school after floods damaged or destroyed nearly 27,000 schools and that it had established more than 500 temporary learning centres and supported teachers and children with supplies.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Sharif is directly tied to the relief and recovery decisions, but implementation depended heavily on BISP, NDMA, provinces, and external partners. The dossier supports real prime-ministerial responsibility, mostly in crisis response.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would require evidence that the recovery framework had already translated into broad, durable improvements for flood-affected households by year-end. I did not go lower because a lower score would miss the scale and speed of the flood-relief response and the direct prime-ministerial instructions behind it.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The court acquittal in the money-laundering case materially weakens the strongest direct corruption allegation against Sharif.
The judge's finding of no nexus between the alleged benami accounts and Sharif or his son is a concrete legal mitigation.
The Daily Mail apology and retraction further reduce one major public corruption allegation.
The public asset disclosure provides direct transparency evidence about his own finances.
The appointment of a technocratic finance minister signals some competence-oriented staffing at the start of his tenure.
The central-bank governor appointment also points to a professional staffing choice in a key institution.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The appointment of Ahad Cheema, a controversial insider with past corruption baggage, keeps the patronage concern alive.
Asset disclosure is positive, but it also shows substantial family-linked wealth and liabilities that keep scrutiny relevant.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: No structured local priors were collected. Pakistan's crisis conditions are context only; the score depends on Sharif's own acquittal, disclosures, and appointments versus the patronage question around insiders.
judge.ruler_attribution: Moderately strong on legal vindication in one major corruption case and on personal disclosure, but not clean enough to erase patronage concerns around appointments. The personal-benefit question is softened more than eliminated.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The insider appointment is a real counterweight against a clean score.
Disclosure helps transparency but does not end scrutiny.

judge.source_mix: Court reporting, public disclosure coverage, and Reuters-syndicated appointment reporting. Strongest on legal outcome and self-disclosure; weaker on long-run personal-benefit proof.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Local priors unavailable in this experiment; judgment uses only the embedded dossier.
judge.chapter_rationale: Sharif scores in the middle because the dossier contains a real acquittal, a judicial finding that there was no nexus to the alleged accounts, a public asset disclosure, and several technocratic appointments. Those are meaningful integrity positives. The negative side is a clear insider appointment and the fact that family-linked wealth remains visible rather than trivial. That is enough to keep the score from climbing into the 6s or 7s, but not enough to push it down into the low end.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score below 4 would ignore the acquittal and the judge's explicit no-nexus finding. Those matter substantially.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score above 6 would treat one acquittal as if it resolved the broader patronage and family-allegation environment. The dossier does not go that far.
judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Shehbaz Sharif's record on integrity in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: A special court acquitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Hamza Shehbaz in the Rs16 billion money laundering case after the FIA told the court that no direct transaction had been made from benami accounts into their bank accounts; and The trial judge said the record was silent on any benefit to Shehbaz Sharif or Hamza from the alleged benami accounts, found no nexus between them and the accounts, and said there was no probability of conviction.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: On the prime minister's advice, Ahad Cheema was appointed adviser to the PM on establishment; the report also notes his prior NAB arrest and inquiries linked to Ashiana-i-Iqbal and related cases; and The ECP data released in 2022 showed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's assets at about Rs246 million, including London property, a small bank balance, liabilities, and a loan from his son Suleman.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Moderately strong on legal vindication in one major corruption case and on personal disclosure, but not clean enough to erase patronage concerns around appointments. The personal-benefit question is softened more than eliminated.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score above 6 would treat one acquittal as if it resolved the broader patronage and family-allegation environment. The dossier does not go that far. I did not go lower because a score below 4 would ignore the acquittal and the judge's explicit no-nexus finding. Those matter substantially.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister and tasked him with quickly arresting the economic spiral and restarting IMF talks.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif's coalition government; the appointment was made by Sharif, though the economic crisis was inherited and IMF constraints remained external.
contrary_evidence: This appointment alone does not prove later policy quality or implementation.

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget speech from the finance ministry with explicit policy commitments.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Sharif's government and budget team; some wording is rhetorical, but it reflects the government's public policy line.
contrary_evidence: Speech rhetoric can overstate intent relative to later execution.

evidence.claim: The FY2022-23 budget was framed as a sustainable-growth budget built around widening the tax net, reducing the fiscal deficit, protecting vulnerable groups, continuing the IMF programme, targeting subsidies, and increasing taxes on wealthy people.

evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and the FY2022-23 policy cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government policy under Sharif's coalition; broader macro conditions and IMF constraints are separate from the ruler's stated priorities.
contrary_evidence: It is a plan document, so implementation has to be checked elsewhere.

evidence.claim: Pakistan appointed career central banker Jameel Ahmad as governor of the State Bank of Pakistan for a five-year term, and he was expected to chair a monetary-policy meeting soon after taking office.

evidence.ruler_attribution: The governor was appointed by the Sharif government, but the SBP remained an institutionally separate actor.
contrary_evidence: Appointment quality does not by itself prove the quality of later monetary policy.

evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target period and after the first half-year of Sharif's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sharif's coalition and party leadership choices; the precise degree of PM autonomy is partly obscured by party-family dynamics.
contrary_evidence: The resignation also reflects coalition and party politics rather than a clean managerial judgment.

evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct PM action, though coalition bargaining limited full control.
contrary_evidence: Coalition partners had divergent views on timing and priorities.

evidence.claim: The finance minister said the new government would cut expenditures and development funds to revive the IMF programme.
evidence.title: Pakistan to cut expenditures, development funds to revive IMF programme

evidence.claim: Pakistan took important measures, and the IMF prioritized steadfast FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, social safety, and SOE/governance reforms.

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release with program details and official approval outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but mediated by the IMF program and inherited macro crisis.
contrary_evidence: The same release says FY22 policies produced overheating, deficits, and reserve erosion.

evidence.claim: The PDNA estimated large flood damages and reconstruction needs, called for a poor-first, transparent, inclusive recovery, and said the government was providing immediate relief while aiming at macroeconomic stability.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Flood Damages and Economic Losses Over USD 30 billion and Reconstruction Needs Over USD 16 billion - New Assessment
evidence.excerpt: The PDNA estimated large flood damages and reconstruction needs, called for a poor-first, transparent, inclusive recovery, and said the government was providing immediate relief while aiming at macroeconomic stability.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank assessment with explicit recovery principles and quantified damage estimates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable through government relief design and response, but heavily constrained by disaster magnitude and donor reliance.
contrary_evidence: The assessment says losses and poverty impacts were still increasing and external support would be essential.

evidence.claim: Five World Bank projects supported flood recovery, housing reconstruction, crop restoration, social protection delivery, and health services for mothers and children, including cash transfers and strengthened disaster-response capacity.
evidence.title: Pakistan: World Bank Approves $1.692 Billion for 5 Projects to Support the People of Sindh in the Flood-Affected Areas
evidence.excerpt: Five World Bank projects supported flood recovery, housing reconstruction, crop restoration, social protection delivery, and health services for mothers and children, including cash transfers and strengthened disaster-response capacity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank announcement with concrete project terms and funding amounts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant: the Sharif government was the implementing counterpart, though execution depended on the Bank and provinces.
contrary_evidence: This is implementation architecture more than proof of completed outcomes by year-end.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Sharif's first finance appointment shows immediate crisis-oriented executive action.
The coalition cabinet and IMF restart focus show direct political mobilization at the start of his tenure.
The budget's fiscal tightening and tax increases show concrete, if constrained, policy action.
The flood recovery framework shows organized medium-term crisis management rather than mere rhetoric.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Finance-minister turnover within months suggests internal friction and unstable economic management.
IMF surveillance shows Pakistan under severe macro stress and still requiring substantial external discipline.
Flood recovery projects were important but still largely prospective by year-end.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Sharif inherited a severe balance-of-payments and inflation crisis, plus flood devastation, and a coalition with limited room for maneuver. The dossier shows real emergency management and policy tightening, but much of the economic program is still framed as crisis repair rather than durable transformation.
judge.ruler_attribution: Moderate: Sharif clearly drove the coalition and crisis response, but the IMF, provinces, and inherited macro emergency strongly shaped the result. The record is better than mere survival, but weaker than a clean, independently audited turnaround.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Key finance leadership changed quickly, which points to instability and contested control.
The IMF program underscores how much external constraint remained.
Flood reconstruction and social projects were still incomplete by year-end.

judge.source_mix: Reuters, finance ministry documents, PID, IMF, and World Bank. Strong on crisis management and policy intent, but outcome evidence remains partial and donor-mediated.
judge.structured_prior_summary: No structured local priors were collected. The dossier supports a middling competence score with substantial crisis-context caveats.
judge.chapter_rationale: Sharif scores as a cautious, crisis-bound manager. He moved quickly to form a coalition cabinet, restart IMF talks, tighten the budget, and launch a flood recovery framework. Those are real governing acts, and they show more than passive inheritance. But the leadership changed rapidly, the economy remained deeply constrained, and a number of core outcomes were still prospective or externally supervised. That is enough for moderate competence, not enough for a high score.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the real emergency coordination, fiscal action, and recovery planning visible in the dossier.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not justified because the macro situation remained fragile, leadership turnover was high, and durable outcomes were not yet visible.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects crisis execution, not approval of the coalition's policy choices.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Shehbaz Sharif's record on effectiveness in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 5.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Shehbaz Sharif appointed economist and businessman Miftah Ismail as finance minister and tasked him with quickly arresting the economic spiral and restarting IMF talks; and Shehbaz Sharif appointed a multi-party coalition cabinet that immediately focused on stabilizing the economy and restarting IMF talks.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Miftah Ismail resigned as finance minister, clearing the way for Ishaq Dar to take over after months of internal pressure about key economic decisions, especially fuel prices; and Pakistan took important measures, and the IMF prioritized steadfast FY23 budget implementation, a market-determined exchange rate, prudent monetary policy, social safety, and SOE/governance reforms.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Moderate: Sharif clearly drove the coalition and crisis response, but the IMF, provinces, and inherited macro emergency strongly shaped the result. The record is better than mere survival, but weaker than a clean, independently audited turnaround.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score is not justified because the macro situation remained fragile, leadership turnover was high, and durable outcomes were not yet visible. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the real emergency coordination, fiscal action, and recovery planning visible in the dossier.

evidence.claim: In December 2022 Nigeria hosted an IAEA-backed SEED workshop to build capacity for site safety evaluation for a first nuclear power plant, with two sites selected and feasibility work underway.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The president-approved NNRA regulations are a concrete institutional safety step attributable to Buhari.
The IAEA safeguards inspection in June 2022 provides real compliance activity inside the nuclear safety system.
The SEED workshop shows active preparatory safety governance for future nuclear installation review.
Nigeria's treaty and safeguards posture reinforces peaceful use and verification norms.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The IAEA country sheet is a status record, not proof of effective day-to-day compliance or implementation.
The NNRA statement is partly self-descriptive and therefore stronger on posture than on verified performance.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Nigeria is a non-nuclear state with a civil-nuclear regulatory framework and treaty commitments. Buhari's role was mainly regulatory stewardship, not nuclear command, so the score should reflect institutional maintenance rather than crisis management.
judge.ruler_attribution: The clearest 2022 ruler-attributed fact is approval of nuclear regulations. The rest of the file is state-regulatory or inspection context that supports, but does not fully prove, strong performance.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Status records and self-description are useful but do not establish implementation quality.
The regime is peaceful, but the file does not give an independent audit of effectiveness.

judge.source_mix: Official regulator and treaty records dominate, with no local priors. The mix is strong on formal safety posture and weaker on audited outcomes, which is exactly why the score sits in the middle rather than the high bands.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected for this experiment; all lens rows are marked not_available.
judge.chapter_rationale: Buhari's chapter record is modestly positive because the government approved nuclear regulations, hosted an IAEA safeguards inspection, and ran a safety-capacity workshop for future nuclear installation review. These are concrete safety and verification actions, but the file is still more about institutional posture than proved outcome. That makes the score respectable but not especially high.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the fact that the file contains concrete regulatory and inspection activity in the target year.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require independent outcome audits or a more direct commander-level role than the dossier provides.

chapter_specific.value: Civil-nuclear regulatory state with treaty commitments, not a weapons posture.
Legally stronger, but not independently proven to be better in practice.
Direct approval exists for some regulations; much of the rest is institutional context.
No crisis is shown; the record is about oversight and preparedness.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on nuclear and existential responsibility in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 5.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The page says Buhari approved five NNRA regulations covering safeguards, research reactors, physical protection, nuclear power plant siting, and uranium mining, and that he is chairman of the NNRA governing board; and IAEA safeguards inspectors visited Nigeria on 27-28 June 2022 for physical inventory verification, and the page says the inspection was satisfactory and consistent with Nigeria's safeguards obligations.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Nigeria has an IAEA comprehensive safeguards agreement in force and an Additional Protocol on the record, with nuclear physical protection and liability-related agreements also listed; and Nigeria is described as a party to the NPT, CSA, Additional Protocol, Pelindaba Treaty, and CTBT, and the NNRA says it provides IAEA reporting and domestic inspections to keep material in peaceful use.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: The clearest 2022 ruler-attributed fact is approval of nuclear regulations. The rest of the file is state-regulatory or inspection context that supports, but does not fully prove, strong performance.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would require independent outcome audits or a more direct commander-level role than the dossier provides. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the fact that the file contains concrete regulatory and inspection activity in the target year.

judge.chapter_rationale: Muhammadu Buhari's 2022 Chapter 2B record is not defensibly judgeable from the provided dossier. The only cited material is a long-standing NPT baseline, which establishes Nigeria's inherited legal environment but does not show a 2022 ruler-period peace, war, restraint, or security decision. Because the chapter requires documented target-period international conduct, the correct output is null rather than a fabricated midpoint.

judge.reader_abstract: The available evidence does not support a responsible overall rating of Muhammadu Buhari's international peace in 2022. The dossier contains only an inherited NPT baseline and no defensible 2022 target-period international-security conduct attributable to Buhari, so a numeric Chapter 2B score is not defensible. This is an evidence limitation, not a finding of either good or poor performance; the record remains unscored until stronger ruler-attributed evidence is available.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The official rights report documents killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary arrest, and weak accountability under Buhari's administration.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Nigeria's security environment was already highly violent and decentralized; the score reflects Buhari's responsibility for restraint, remedy, and tolerated impunity rather than all insurgent or communal violence.
judge.ruler_attribution: Mixed: direct for speeches and some security instructions, indirect for many abusive acts by security services and local actors.

contrary_evidence.explanation: He condemned a mob killing and called for investigation.

judge.source_mix: Official state statements, U.S. government reporting, Amnesty, HRW, and Reuters-style current affairs; no client matrix used.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were unavailable across the lens set, so the score is grounded in the cited evidence and the contrary notes embedded in the dossier.
judge.chapter_rationale: Nigeria under Buhari is a recurring-failure case. The record contains serious killings, disappearances, torture, media intimidation, protest repression, and weak accountability, but it is not a clean terror state. Buhari also issued several restraint signals: he condemned mob violence, explicitly rejected lethal force in a hostage crisis, ordered the armed forces to stay apolitical, and urged peaceful grievance handling. Those positives keep the score above the harsh authoritarian floor, but the continued pattern of abuse and impunity keeps it well below a genuinely protective order. The chapter answer is therefore a middling-low score rather than a collapse or a success story.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: I rejected 2-3 because there are repeated restraint statements and some limited legal pressure, so the case is not a pure coercive breakdown.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: I rejected 5+ because the evidence still shows recurring torture, killings, protest suppression, and weak remedy.

chapter_specific.value: recurring and partly systemic in security practice
weak; remedies are partial and often come after public pressure
strained; journalists and critics faced harassment and censorship pressure
some restraint rhetoric, but no durable safety improvement
moderate to high for the federal security environment, but many abuses are operationally decentralized
3B.3 incitement is not the main story; the chapter turns on detention, protest, and remedy failures

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on domestic safety in 2022 was assessed as poor, resulting in a score of 3.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The report lists credible reports of unlawful and arbitrary killings, forced disappearances, torture by government, arbitrary arrest, serious restrictions on expression and media, and weak accountability for major abuses; and Security services reportedly committed torture and inhuman treatment of suspects, detainees, and prisoners, and Amnesty documented 62 cases of arbitrary arrest, ill-treatment, and torture in southeastern states.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Buhari condemned mob violence and called for an impartial probe, which is a restraint signal; and Buhari said lethal military force was considered for the Kaduna train hostages but was reluctantly discarded because collateral damage could not be assured, and he said his primary concern was to get everyone released safe and unhurt.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed: direct for speeches and some security instructions, indirect for many abusive acts by security services and local actors.

Taken together, I did not go higher because I rejected 5+ because the evidence still shows recurring torture, killings, protest suppression, and weak remedy. I did not go lower because I rejected 2-3 because there are repeated restraint statements and some limited legal pressure, so the case is not a pure coercive breakdown.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The Electoral Act 2022 is a real institutional reform that aimed to improve electoral integrity and reduce money politics.
Buhari's pledge to oversee a peaceful, transparent transfer in 2023 is direct evidence of transfer-rule respect.
His statement that the elections would be free, fair, and credible, together with praise for not pursuing a third term, supports a positive transfer-rule reading.
The absence of a preferred successor signal is modest but relevant evidence of not trying to personalize succession.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The Twitter suspension and subsequent legal dispute show speech control and executive pressure on online expression.
State violence and intimidation against peaceful protesters and families of the disappeared undercut the freedom score materially.
Police suppression of supporters of an ousted opponent shows coercive crowd control and political intimidation.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Nigeria in 2022 remained a noisy competitive system with real elections, but security agencies, speech restrictions, and intimidation of journalists and protesters kept political freedom uneven. Buhari also governed within a setting marked by military influence and legacy insecurity.
judge.ruler_attribution: Mixed: the dossier contains several direct Buhari statements and actions, but many coercive acts are carried out by agencies or the wider state apparatus rather than by him personally.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The Electoral Act and transfer rhetoric are real positives and keep the score above the low-authoritarian range.
Buhari's explicit rejection of a third term is a meaningful restraint on personal entrenchment.

judge.source_mix: Mostly official State House speeches and legal announcements, plus Reuters, Amnesty, RSF, and HRW. The mix is good on transfer rules and speech control, but some abuse items are broader state-environment claims rather than directly presidential orders.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment; the judge relied entirely on the embedded projection and its cited evidence.
judge.chapter_rationale: Muhammadu Buhari's 2022 Nigeria is a midrange case. He made notable pro-transfer and pro-election statements, signed an Electoral Act intended to improve integrity, and rejected any third-term logic. At the same time, the year still featured Twitter restrictions, protest suppression, journalist intimidation, and broader rights abuses. That means Nigeria was not closing into authoritarianism, but political freedom remained uneven and vulnerable. The score lands in the middle because the positive transfer-rule evidence is real, yet it coexists with persistent coercion and weak protection for critics.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the Electoral Act, the no-third-term posture, and the fact that Nigeria still had meaningful though imperfect contestability.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would discount the substantial evidence of speech restrictions, protest suppression, and harassment of journalists and activists.

chapter_specific.value: Mixed with modest improvement on succession, but persistent coercion kept political freedom uneven.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on political freedom in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 5.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Buhari signed the Electoral Act 2022, and the presidential release says it was intended to limit money politics and incumbent advantage, while being drafted with civil society, labor, media, and INEC consultation; and Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: SERAP went to court to force publication of the Twitter agreement because it feared the terms could jeopardize freedom of expression, and the government had suspended Twitter after Buhari's tweet was deleted; and VOA Hausa reported Buhari warning the APC that lack of unity and selfishness could cost it the 2023 election, framing internal democracy and coalition discipline as necessary for success.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed: the dossier contains several direct Buhari statements and actions, but many coercive acts are carried out by agencies or the wider state apparatus rather than by him personally.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would discount the substantial evidence of speech restrictions, protest suppression, and harassment of journalists and activists. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the Electoral Act, the no-third-term posture, and the fact that Nigeria still had meaningful though imperfect contestability.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The health-insurance law was a concrete pro-poor policy move.
Anti-money-laundering and proceeds-of-crime laws strengthened the legal framework.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Inflation, poverty, and subsidy burdens remained severe.
Regressive fuel and FX subsidies crowded out pro-poor spending.
The IMF said the oil-price opportunity was not harnessed and governance fixes were still needed.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Nigeria entered 2022 with subsidy distortions, low revenue, inflation pressure, and a weak external position. Those inherited problems were severe, but the score reflects whether the presidency managed them competently and fairly.
judge.ruler_attribution: Attribution is moderate: Buhari clearly set fiscal, legal, and appointment choices, but much of the crisis was inherited and some key levers were constrained by oil theft, subsidies, and exchange-rate rigidity.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The macro and welfare situation was plainly deteriorating.
Subsidies and low revenue were a structural drag on development.

judge.source_mix: World Bank and IMF surveillance, official government acts, central-bank policy records, and Reuters-based reporting; no structured local priors were collected in this experiment.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were unavailable across all lenses; the judgment relies on the dossier evidence and the source-confidence metadata only.
judge.chapter_rationale: Buhari scores 2.5 because the year was still dominated by subsidy distortions, high inflation, poverty pressure, and poor use of fiscal room. There were some genuine reforms, including better legal tools and a modest technocratic appointment, but they were too small to offset the broad economic drag or to show durable correction. The evidence points to a weak, crisis-ridden prosperity record with only limited institutional positives.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score near 1 would ignore the real though limited legal and institutional reforms in the dossier.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score near 3.5 would overstate the strength of the pro-poor and macro-stabilization record relative to the scale of the crisis.

chapter_specific.value: The trajectory was downward or stagnant overall, with reforms too small to reverse the macro drag.
Oil-price and exchange-rate pressures mattered, but the subsidy structure and policy mix were also self-inflicted constraints.
Household welfare was squeezed by inflation and subsidy distortion; the pro-poor legal moves did not materially change that picture in 2022.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on economic well-being in 2022 was assessed as poor, resulting in a score of 2.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill and said a fund would be created to cover 83 million poor Nigerians who cannot afford premiums, with a vulnerable-group fund and data systems to support implementation; and Buhari signed three bills on money laundering, terrorism prevention, and proceeds of crime, saying they were part of the administration's fight against corruption and illicit financing.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: By late 2022 the World Bank said Nigeria's economy was still held back by business-as-usual management, inflation had surged to 21.1 percent, as many as five million more Nigerians had been pushed into poverty, and the petrol subsidy was likely to exceed five trillion naira, while reforms were needed to restore macro stability, broaden private investment, and expand social protection; and The World Bank says Nigeria financed inefficient and regressive petrol, electricity, and foreign-exchange subsidies that benefited mainly wealthy households, cost more than education, health, and social protection spending in 2021, and crowded out pro-poor programs while revenue and spending stayed very low.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Attribution is moderate: Buhari clearly set fiscal, legal, and appointment choices, but much of the crisis was inherited and some key levers were constrained by oil theft, subsidies, and exchange-rate rigidity.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score near 3.5 would overstate the strength of the pro-poor and macro-stabilization record relative to the scale of the crisis. I did not go lower because a score near 1 would ignore the real though limited legal and institutional reforms in the dossier.

evidence.claim: WHO reported that Nigeria ranked first among zero-dose countries in 2022 with over 2.3 million estimated zero-dose children, that the government prioritized reaching these communities in its national immunization and PHC strategy, and that data-targeted collaboration helped reach millions of children with immunization services.

evidence.excerpt: WHO reported that Nigeria ranked first among zero-dose countries in 2022 with over 2.3 million estimated zero-dose children, that the government prioritized reaching these communities in its national immunization and PHC strategy, and that data-targeted collaboration helped reach millions of children with immunization services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO results-report country story with target-year estimates and explicit system responses, albeit published retrospectively.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospectively describes 2022 health-access conditions and the 2020-2023 response period overlapping Buhari's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Buhari's administration through national strategy and PHC system oversight, but implementation was shared with WHO, UNICEF, and subnational actors.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The National Health Insurance Authority law and fund are concrete institutional welfare reforms.
The administration reported large-scale school feeding, health, and cash-support delivery figures.
The humanitarian and social-development framework named several national social programs and target groups.
Joint evaluation found the social-protection program reduced burdens and encouraged care-seeking.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The World Bank described very low public spending and poor development outcomes as structural constraints.
Nigeria remained the top zero-dose country, showing severe immunization exclusion.
A long university strike kept students out of classrooms and signaled weak service delivery.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Nigeria in 2022 faced entrenched poverty, low public spending, insecurity, and service fragmentation. That baseline means some program delivery deserves credit, but the chapter still reads as constrained and incomplete rather than genuinely transformative.
judge.ruler_attribution: The dossier contains substantial government self-reporting, but much of the evidence is at ministry or program level rather than a direct Buhari personal record. His responsibility is real, yet the human-development effect is modest and uneven.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Very low public spending and weak human capital undercut the welfare narrative.
Large zero-dose immunization gaps show that major exclusions persisted.

judge.source_mix: Official Nigerian government releases combined with World Bank, WHO, UNICEF, and WFP material. The dossier is strong on scale claims but weaker on independent audit and durability.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment, so the judgment relies on the embedded dossier evidence, the reviewer exclusions already present there, and cross-case calibration within the batch.
judge.chapter_rationale: Buhari gets a low-middling score because the record contains real institutional welfare reforms and some large program numbers, but the broader picture remains one of weak public spending, major immunization exclusion, and persistent service breakdown. The good evidence is not imaginary, yet it is outweighed by the scale of deprivation and the thinness of independent outcome verification. That places the dossier below the middle band but not in outright failure territory.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the fact that there were substantive health and social-protection reforms and some positive evaluation of relief programs.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require stronger evidence that these programs materially overcame Nigeria's severe baseline deficits in 2022.

chapter_specific.value: health insurance, school feeding, cash support, humanitarian relief, immunization
poor and indigent Nigerians, children, and displaced communities are targeted, but exclusion remains large
insecurity, strikes, and low spending shape the welfare story
some genuine institutional gains, but severe coverage gaps and weak execution

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on social well-being in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022, said a fund would be created to cover 83 million poor Nigerians who cannot afford premiums, and said the new law would support digital records, data collection, and monitoring; and The administration reported large-scale school feeding, health, and cash-support delivery figures.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: The World Bank said Nigeria spent only about 220 dollars per person in 2022, social sectors received less than a quarter of the national budget, and low public spending translated into poor development outcomes and weak human capital; and WHO reported that Nigeria ranked first among zero-dose countries in 2022 with over 2.3 million estimated zero-dose children, that the government prioritized reaching these communities in its national immunization and PHC strategy, and that data-targeted collaboration helped reach millions of children with immunization services.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: The dossier contains substantial government self-reporting, but much of the evidence is at ministry or program level rather than a direct Buhari personal record. His responsibility is real, yet the human-development effect is modest and uneven.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would require stronger evidence that these programs materially overcame Nigeria's severe baseline deficits in 2022. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the fact that there were substantive health and social-protection reforms and some positive evaluation of relief programs.
