evidence.claim: Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Democracy Day Speech
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech with explicit transition and contestability language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari.
contrary_evidence: This is rhetoric and self-presentation, not proof of actual electoral conduct.
The speech does not by itself rule out manipulation elsewhere in the system.

evidence.claim: Buhari said fighting corruption remained a cardinal pillar of the administration, linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, and said ICPC should continue investigating sexual harassment in educational institutions.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the 4th National Summit on Diminishing Corruption in the Public Sector
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said fighting corruption remained a cardinal pillar of the administration, linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, and said ICPC should continue investigating sexual harassment in educational institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript; reliable for what he said, but self-report and not independent proof of practice.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari statement; strong attribution for rhetoric and commitments, weak for actual adherence.
contrary_evidence: Later 2022 nominations of loyal aides and relatives undercut the anti-nepotism and anti-patronage framing.

evidence.claim: Buhari directed cabinet members contesting elective office to resign by May 16, 2022 so they would not unfairly benefit from their government positions.
evidence.title: Nigeria’s Buhari asks ministers with political ambition to resign
evidence.excerpt: Buhari directed cabinet members contesting elective office to resign by May 16, 2022 so they would not unfairly benefit from their government positions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated report on a concrete directive and resulting resignations; strong for the fact of the rule, not for motive.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 during the election-cycle conflict-of-interest window.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari directive through his information minister; strong nexus to control of office and conflict separation.
contrary_evidence: The rule covered ministers only, not all appointees, so it did not eliminate broader patronage risks.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Buhari had no preferred APC successor and had anointed no one, and that he would step down in 2023 after eight years in office.
evidence.title: Nigeria: Buhari has no preferred successor, spokesman says
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Buhari had no preferred APC successor and had anointed no one, and that he would step down in 2023 after eight years in office.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a specific public statement by the president's spokesman; strong for the public commitment itself.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 ahead of the succession contest.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Buhari through his spokesman; evidence supports a public non-anointment commitment, not hidden internal intent.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not prove he exerted no behind-the-scenes influence, only that he denied having a preferred candidate.

evidence.claim: The article says Buhari had appointed several family members and close relatives, and specifically notes that in September 2022 Ahmed Halilu, Aisha Buhari's brother, was appointed managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company.
evidence.title: Buhari's actions contradict nepotism comment
evidence.excerpt: The article says Buhari had appointed several family members and close relatives, and specifically notes that in September 2022 Ahmed Halilu, Aisha Buhari's brother, was appointed managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Published commentary with a concrete appointment and family tie; the underlying appointment is corroborable, though the article is not a formal finding of illegality.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to Buhari's appointing power.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment; strong nexus to Buhari's control over senior posts, though personal enrichment is not shown.
contrary_evidence: The article acknowledges that the president had constitutional discretion to appoint qualified people, so the appointment alone does not prove corruption or illegality.

evidence.claim: Buhari nominated his Special Assistant on Social Media, Lauretta Onochie, as substantive chair of the Niger Delta Development Commission and asked the Senate to confirm the appointment.
evidence.title: Buhari Nominates Lauretta Onochie As NDDC Chair, 14 Other Board Members
evidence.excerpt: Buhari nominated his Special Assistant on Social Media, Lauretta Onochie, as substantive chair of the Niger Delta Development Commission and asked the Senate to confirm the appointment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct report of a concrete nomination with clear job history, strong for the appointment fact and loyalty nexus.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari nomination; the appointee was a close political aide, so the loyalty/patronage nexus is strong.
contrary_evidence: Onochie later denied partisan membership and supporters argued she was qualified, so the nomination is not itself proof of illegality.

evidence.claim: Buhari said weapons from the Ukraine-Russia war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad Basin, but VOA's fact check found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports or evidence supporting it.
evidence.title: Unsubstantiated: Buhari Claim That Ukraine War Feeds Arms to West Africa
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said weapons from the Ukraine-Russia war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad Basin, but VOA's fact check found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports or evidence supporting it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct quote plus explicit fact-check with sourcing discussion; strong for the unsupported-claim assessment, weaker on intent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari public statement; the fact check challenges the claim's evidentiary basis but cannot prove deliberate deception.
contrary_evidence: There is independent evidence of regional arms diversion from stockpiles and battlefield capture, but not of the specific Ukraine-to-Lake-Chad route Buhari asserted.

evidence.claim: Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu as substantive managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company, after Halilu had served in an acting role; the report says the appointment followed a CBN governor recommendation.
evidence.title: Buhari appoints Ahmed Halilu NSPMC MD
evidence.excerpt: Buhari approved Ahmed Halilu as substantive managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company, after Halilu had served in an acting role; the report says the appointment followed a CBN governor recommendation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous report with specific names and office, but secondary and dependent on unnamed CBN source.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and about a 2022 appointment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari because the article says he approved the appointment; the CBN recommendation limits inference about sole presidential authorship.
contrary_evidence: Does not by itself prove nepotistic intent or personal benefit.
The report attributes the recommendation to the CBN governor and gives Halilu prior acting experience.

evidence.claim: The report says Ahmed Halilu, the elder brother to First Lady Aisha Buhari, was appointed managing director of NSPMC and that Buhari made the appointment permanent after Halilu had acted since May 16, 2022.
evidence.title: Buhari appoints brother-in-law, Ahmed Halilu, to head Nigeria's currency printing company
evidence.excerpt: The report says Ahmed Halilu, the elder brother to First Lady Aisha Buhari, was appointed managing director of NSPMC and that Buhari made the appointment permanent after Halilu had acted since May 16, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report with a concrete family relationship and appointment fact, though it is still secondary reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Buhari because the article states he made the appointment permanent; family relationship supports a nepotism reading but does not prove personal gain.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes Halilu's prior acting role and reported CBN backing, which support a competence-based explanation.
It does not show Buhari personally profited from the appointment.

evidence.claim: Buhari said weapons used in the Russia-Ukraine war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad region and warned that the illegal movement of arms was heightening the proliferation of small arms and light weapons.
evidence.title: President Buhari Calls for Tighter Security Around Borders in Lake Chad Basin with the Proliferation of Weapons from Russia-Ukraine War
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said weapons used in the Russia-Ukraine war were beginning to filter into the Lake Chad region and warned that the illegal movement of arms was heightening the proliferation of small arms and light weapons.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential press release quoting Buhari directly on the disputed claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari because this is his quoted public statement, though it does not itself prove the factual claim was true.
contrary_evidence: VOA later found the claim unsubstantiated and noted there were no public reports supporting it.
I did not locate any public correction by Buhari in the searched record.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The family appointment of Ahmed Halilu into the currency-printing company is a concrete nepotism signal.
The nomination of Lauretta Onochie, a close aide, to lead the NDDC is another direct loyalty-based appointment.
The permanent approval of Ahmed Halilu's appointment reinforces the family-network concern.
The brother-in-law framing makes the patronage nexus even clearer, though it still does not prove personal gain.
The unsupported Ukraine-to-Lake-Chad claim is a direct public statement that was fact-checked as unsubstantiated.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The instruction for ministers seeking office to resign is a real anti-conflict measure.
The Democratic Day speech promises a peaceful transfer and denounces violence, which is a genuine public commitment to transition.
The anti-corruption speech and procurement-transparency emphasis are not proof of success, but they are real accountability language.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: No structured local priors were collected. Nigeria's corruption and insecurity context is background only; the score turns on Buhari's own directives, family-linked appointments, and unsupported public claim.
judge.ruler_attribution: Direct on the family appointments and the unsupported claim, but only partially on overall patronage because some appointees were also described as qualified. The dossier shows mixed integrity with a clear nepotism pattern, not a fully proven personal enrichment case.

contrary_evidence.explanation: A real anti-conflict directive prevents a pure nepotism-only score.
The transition speech is a genuine public commitment, even if rhetoric alone is not enough.

judge.source_mix: Official speeches, Reuters-syndicated reporting, and contemporaneous media reports on appointments. Strongest on what Buhari said and whom he appointed; weaker on final findings of misconduct.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Local priors unavailable in this experiment; judgment relies on the embedded evidence and gap notes only.
judge.chapter_rationale: Buhari lands in the lower middle because the record combines a real anti-conflict directive and transition rhetoric with concrete family and loyalist appointments and one unsupported public claim about Ukraine-derived arms. That is enough to show a mixed but compromised integrity profile. The score does not fall lower because there is also some formal restraint and not every controversial appointment is shown to be illegitimate. It does not rise higher because the family-network pattern is too visible and the unsupported claim is a direct honesty problem.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score below 3 would require a much more settled showing of personal extraction or deliberate lying as the dominant mode of rule. The dossier is troubling but not that complete.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score above 5 would overrate the anti-corruption rhetoric and undercount the family and loyalist appointments. The patronage pattern is real.
judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on integrity in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The article says Buhari had appointed several family members and close relatives, and specifically notes that in September 2022 Ahmed Halilu, Aisha Buhari's brother, was appointed managing director of the Nigerian Security Printing and Minting Company; and Buhari nominated his Special Assistant on Social Media, Lauretta Onochie, as substantive chair of the Niger Delta Development Commission and asked the Senate to confirm the appointment.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Buhari directed cabinet members contesting elective office to resign by May 16, 2022 so they would not unfairly benefit from their government positions; and Buhari said it was his last Democracy Day speech, promised a peaceful and transparent transfer to a new president in 2023, praised 2022 party primaries as peaceful and orderly, and said aggrieved actors sought judicial justice rather than violence.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Direct on the family appointments and the unsupported claim, but only partially on overall patronage because some appointees were also described as qualified. The dossier shows mixed integrity with a clear nepotism pattern, not a fully proven personal enrichment case.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score above 5 would overrate the anti-corruption rhetoric and undercount the family and loyalist appointments. The patronage pattern is real. I did not go lower because a score below 3 would require a much more settled showing of personal extraction or deliberate lying as the dominant mode of rule. The dossier is troubling but not that complete.

evidence.claim: Buhari signed the 2022 Appropriation Bill and 2021 Finance Bill into law, restoring a predictable January-to-December fiscal year, while asking for amendment and virement because the National Assembly had altered many projects and allocations.
evidence.title: President Buhari Signs N17.127tr 2022 Budget Into Law, Directs MDAs to Commence Early Preparation of 2023 Transition Budget
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the 2022 Appropriation Bill and 2021 Finance Bill into law, restoring a predictable January-to-December fiscal year, while asking for amendment and virement because the National Assembly had altered many projects and allocations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official record of the president's fiscal act and stated concerns about budget changes.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 enactment that governed the 2022 fiscal framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler action, though the resulting budget also reflects National Assembly amendments and inherited fiscal constraints.
contrary_evidence: The president said the enacted budget still needed amendment/virement, suggesting implementation friction rather than a clean policy win.

evidence.claim: Buhari approved the appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as NBS Statistician-General and CEO; the notice describes him as a professional statistician with more than three decades of experience and prior NBS leadership roles.
evidence.title: President Buhari Approves Appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as Statistician-General of the Federation and Chief Executive Officer of the National Bureau of Statistics
evidence.excerpt: Buhari approved the appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as NBS Statistician-General and CEO; the notice describes him as a professional statistician with more than three decades of experience and prior NBS leadership roles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official appointment notice with a direct attribution and a specific technocratic résumé.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 appointment relevant to data capacity and evidence-based policy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler action, though one technocratic appointment does not prove the quality of the broader economic team.
contrary_evidence: A single technocratic appointment does not offset other evidence of politicization in economic offices.

evidence.claim: Buhari said cabinet selection had been careful to bring in the best and most competent people, that new members were added to inject fresh energies, skills, and ideas, and that replacements would be made without delay so governance would not suffer.
evidence.title: President Buhari's Speech at the Valedictory Session for Appointees Leaving the Cabinet to Pursue Political Ambition
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said cabinet selection had been careful to bring in the best and most competent people, that new members were added to inject fresh energies, skills, and ideas, and that replacements would be made without delay so governance would not suffer.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official speech, but the competence claim is self-assessment rather than independent verification.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement about cabinet composition and governance continuity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler claim about his own appointments and cabinet management.
contrary_evidence: The speech is self-justifying and does not independently prove competence or depoliticization.

evidence.claim: Buhari framed 2022 tax policy around stable domestic revenue mobilization, tax harmonization, clearer FIRS authority, and improved tax-to-GDP performance, while saying the 2021 tax dialogue influenced policy and administrative changes and FIRS surpassed its 2021 collection target.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Address at the 2nd National Tax Dialogue Week
evidence.excerpt: Buhari framed 2022 tax policy around stable domestic revenue mobilization, tax harmonization, clearer FIRS authority, and improved tax-to-GDP performance, while saying the 2021 tax dialogue influenced policy and administrative changes and FIRS surpassed its 2021 collection target.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential speech, but self-reported success and goals need outside corroboration for execution claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari policy direction through tax administration; execution attribution is partial because outcomes also depend on the revenue authority and broader macro conditions.
contrary_evidence: World Bank and IMF later described Nigeria's revenue base as very weak and fiscal space constrained.
The speech is aspirational and does not itself prove sustained implementation.

evidence.claim: Buhari said his administration's fight against corruption was a cardinal reform pillar and linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, while urging ICPC action on sexual harassment in education.
evidence.title: President Buhari’s Speech at the 4th National Summit on Diminishing Corruption in the Public Sector
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said his administration's fight against corruption was a cardinal reform pillar and linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, while urging ICPC action on sexual harassment in education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Buhari speech with clear stated priorities, but it is mainly rhetoric and only limited execution evidence sits in the speech itself.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari statement and reform signal; actual anti-corruption performance needs independent corroboration.
contrary_evidence: The speech is aspirational and does not by itself show results.
Other evidence shows ongoing corruption and fiscal leakage.

evidence.claim: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022 and said a fund would cover 83 million poor Nigerians, using a vulnerable-group fund, digital records, and state-federal implementation coordination.
evidence.title: In Bid to Achieve Universal Coverage, President Buhari Signs National Health Authority Bill Into Law
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022 and said a fund would cover 83 million poor Nigerians, using a vulnerable-group fund, digital records, and state-federal implementation coordination.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential action with a concrete institutional reform and target population, though delivery still depends on implementation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari enactment through presidential assent; implementation is shared with the health ministry, states, and the new authority.
contrary_evidence: Coverage promises do not prove actual enrollment or service quality in 2022.
The program is partly an institutional design rather than a completed outcome.

evidence.claim: Buhari described the humanitarian ministry as a strategic intervention and listed IDP, flood-response, disability, aging, poverty-reduction, and social-investment frameworks as part of a plan to lift 100 million Nigerians out of poverty in 10 years.
evidence.title: Humanitarian Issues: President Buhari Urges More Private Sector Participation, Highlights Intervention Programmes
evidence.excerpt: Buhari described the humanitarian ministry as a strategic intervention and listed IDP, flood-response, disability, aging, poverty-reduction, and social-investment frameworks as part of a plan to lift 100 million Nigerians out of poverty in 10 years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential account of policy architecture, but most of the evidence is self-description rather than independent evaluation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Buhari framing of the administration's social-protection and humanitarian program; delivery responsibility is shared with the ministry, agencies, states, and partners.
contrary_evidence: The ministry was created in 2019, so much of the structure predates 2022.
A stated framework is not proof of effective delivery.

evidence.claim: ASUU suspended its eight-month strike after appeals from President Buhari and others, and Reuters noted the government had set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.
evidence.title: Nigeria's public university lecturers suspend strike after eight months
evidence.excerpt: ASUU suspended its eight-month strike after appeals from President Buhari and others, and Reuters noted the government had set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.
evidence.source_locator: Reuters report text in article body
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated reporting on a major implementation failure and the government's response; the suspension does not prove the dispute was solved.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Buhari's appeal and budget response are directly attributable, but the strike also reflected entrenched labor disputes and university-funding structure.
contrary_evidence: The union said issues were not satisfactorily resolved.
The dispute had been ongoing for months, so suspension was not full execution of a reform plan.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Signing the budget into law and directing transition preparation shows basic fiscal control and calendar discipline.
The NBS appointment shows at least one technocratic staffing choice consistent with evidence-based administration.
The National Health Authority law is a substantive institutional reform with a defined coverage ambition.
The university-strike suspension and salary-enhancement commitment show some crisis response capacity.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Cabinet self-assessment and turnover reflect more rhetorical competence claims than independent proof of execution.
Anti-corruption framing is aspirational and not matched here by strong independent result evidence.
The humanitarian-poverty framework is broad, but the dossier does not verify delivery quality or outcome change.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Buhari inherited a difficult security and fiscal environment and finished office with limited time to convert plans into outcomes. The 2022 file is heavy on statements, appointments, and formal reforms, but light on independently audited implementation success, especially at household level.
judge.ruler_attribution: Direct on some appointments and legislation, but much of the evidence is self-description and the delivery chain is weak. The result is basic governing control with limited proof of effective execution.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Cabinet praise does not equal independently verified competence.
Anti-corruption and transparency claims are not backed here by strong execution evidence.
The strike resolution was partial and reactive rather than a clean policy success.

judge.source_mix: Mostly official Nigerian government materials with Reuters-syndicated reporting. Strong for formal acts, weaker for independent outcomes and follow-through.
judge.structured_prior_summary: No structured local priors were collected; the dossier supports a low-to-mid competence score with substantial uncertainty on execution quality.
judge.chapter_rationale: Buhari's 2022 record contains some real governing acts: budget signing, a technocratic appointment, a health-authority law, and a response to the university strike. But the dossier is dominated by official self-description and broad frameworks, with relatively little hard evidence that those actions were translated into durable, well-implemented outcomes. That leaves him in the lower-middle band: not inert, but not convincingly effective in turning policy into strong results.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the genuine legislative and appointment actions that did occur in 2022.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not justified because the file lacks strong independent evidence of implementation quality or durable progress.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects execution competence, not approval or disapproval of the administration's agenda.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Muhammadu Buhari's record on effectiveness in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Buhari signed the 2022 Appropriation Bill and 2021 Finance Bill into law, restoring a predictable January-to-December fiscal year, while asking for amendment and virement because the National Assembly had altered many projects and allocations; and Buhari approved the appointment of Semiu Adeyemi Adeniran as NBS Statistician-General and CEO; the notice describes him as a professional statistician with more than three decades of experience and prior NBS leadership roles.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Buhari said cabinet selection had been careful to bring in the best and most competent people, that new members were added to inject fresh energies, skills, and ideas, and that replacements would be made without delay so governance would not suffer; and Buhari said his administration's fight against corruption was a cardinal reform pillar and linked the Open Government Partnership to transparency in public finances and procurement, while urging ICPC action on sexual harassment in education.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Direct on some appointments and legislation, but much of the evidence is self-description and the delivery chain is weak. The result is basic governing control with limited proof of effective execution.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score is not justified because the file lacks strong independent evidence of implementation quality or durable progress. I did not go lower because a lower score would miss the genuine legislative and appointment actions that did occur in 2022.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The ANSN law created an autonomous nuclear-safety regulator, a concrete institutional safeguard attributable to Bolsonaro's signing of the law.
The 2022 decree implemented ANSN's structure and its monitoring, regulation, and inspection mandate.
Promulgation of the physical-protection amendment is a formal nuclear-security step in the target year.
ABACC's safeguards mission and coordination framework reinforce Brazil's peaceful nuclear posture.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Brazil's TPNW status is only a signature, not ratification, so the nonproliferation posture is real but not maximal.
Civil nuclear reactors are a safety-governed context, but not evidence of broader weapons-risk leadership or realized risk reduction.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil entered 2022 with a strong treaty and safeguards baseline, plus a civil nuclear sector rather than a weapons program. Bolsonaro's sphere of responsibility was mostly regulatory and institutional, not crisis-driven nuclear command.
judge.ruler_attribution: The strongest 2022 items are formal executive/legal acts under Bolsonaro's presidency. They do not prove perfect implementation, but they are concrete risk-bearing choices rather than mere rhetoric.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Signature without ratification is weaker than full treaty commitment.
The civil-reactor profile is safety context, not evidence of a broader existential-risk breakthrough.

judge.source_mix: Official legal texts and official institutional pages dominate, with some current-profile context; no local priors were available, but the evidence base is stronger than mere rhetoric because it includes enacted law and decree language.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected for this experiment; all lens rows are marked not_available.
judge.chapter_rationale: Bolsonaro's 2022 record is meaningfully positive because it includes concrete, ruler-attributable nuclear-safety institution building: the ANSN framework, the 2022 implementing decree, and a physical-protection amendment. The limits are equally clear: the dossier is about civil nuclear governance and formal compliance, not a dramatic crisis intervention or a major arms-control advance. That keeps the score below the top bands, but above a merely mixed assessment, because the state did put in place real safeguards under his presidency.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the concrete legal and regulatory actions that improved Brazil's nuclear safety architecture in 2022.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A materially higher score would require evidence of more consequential command, crisis, or implementation gains than the file actually shows.

chapter_specific.value: Peaceful civil-nuclear baseline with treaty and safeguards constraints.
Safer and more formalized nuclear regulation by year-end.
Direct executive and legal attribution exists for the law and decree, though not for day-to-day safety performance.
No crisis episode is shown, but the safety architecture was strengthened in formal terms.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Jair Bolsonaro's record on nuclear and existential responsibility in 2022 was assessed as generally positive, with important limitations, resulting in a score of 6.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The law created the Autoridade Nacional de Segurança Nuclear (ANSN) as an autonomous federal body responsible for monitoring, regulating, and inspecting nuclear safety, radiological protection, and physical security; and The decree implemented ANSN's regimental structure and confirmed that it would monitor, regulate, and inspect nuclear safety, radiological protection, and physical security in Brazil.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Brazil's TPNW status is only a signature, not ratification, so the nonproliferation posture is real but not maximal; and Brazil's profile shows two nuclear power reactors in operation and one under construction, with nuclear power supplying a small share of electricity.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: The strongest 2022 items are formal executive/legal acts under Bolsonaro's presidency. They do not prove perfect implementation, but they are concrete risk-bearing choices rather than mere rhetoric.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a materially higher score would require evidence of more consequential command, crisis, or implementation gains than the file actually shows. I did not go lower because a lower score would miss the concrete legal and regulatory actions that improved Brazil's nuclear safety architecture in 2022.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Bolsonaro publicly said Brazil would remain neutral and not take sides, which is restraint compared with open alignment in the Ukraine war.
Brazil's UN statement urged diplomatic solutions and expressed grave concern about Russian military operations.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The Moscow visit days before the invasion, including talk of Russian nuclear reactors, looks politically tone-deaf and not strongly peace-promoting.
Brazil abstained on the annexation resolution, which is more cautious than a clear accountability vote.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil was not a belligerent and had limited leverage over the war, so the key question is whether Bolsonaro chose clear restraint or merely avoided direct alignment.
judge.ruler_attribution: The strongest items are government and direct Bolsonaro statements; the posture is attributable to his administration even when the language comes through ministers or the UN mission.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The Moscow state visit undercut the clarity of Brazil's anti-aggression posture.
Procedural caution at the UN reflected legal hedging, not strong peace leadership.

judge.source_mix: Official Brazilian releases, UN records, and Reuters-based reporting provide the core evidence; local priors were unavailable in this experiment.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment; the judgment uses the embedded dossier evidence and chapter-level counterevidence only.
judge.chapter_rationale: Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 record is mixed rather than clearly aggressive or clearly exemplary. Brazil took real peace-oriented positions on Ukraine, including diplomacy, humanitarian protection, and some legal accountability language, but Bolsonaro also made a conspicuous pre-invasion trip to Moscow, voiced neutrality instead of stronger condemnation, and repeatedly chose caution over leadership at the UN. That supports a midpoint score: better than acquiescence, but not strong enough to count as robust peace leadership.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score of 4 is too low because Brazil did support diplomacy, humanitarian protection, and UN accountability positions on Ukraine.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score of 6 is too high because the record remains hedged, with neutrality language, abstentions, and a questionable Moscow signal before the invasion.

chapter_specific.value: Mixed restraint: some humanitarian and legal positioning, but undermined by neutrality and a risky pre-invasion Moscow trip.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Jair Bolsonaro's record on international peace in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Bolsonaro said Brazil would remain neutral in the Russia-Ukraine war and would not take sides, adding that the conflict was not Brazil's problem; and Brazil said the Security Council should pursue diplomatic solutions to the Ukraine crisis and expressed grave concern about Russian military operations against Ukrainian territory.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: During a Moscow visit, Bolsonaro said Brazil was interested in small nuclear reactors from Rosatom and said, 'We pray for peace,' while not mentioning Ukraine by name; and Brazil abstained on the annexation resolution, saying its calls for a cessation of hostilities and return to dialogue were not included and warning that any use of nuclear weapons would be catastrophic for humanity.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: The strongest items are government and direct Bolsonaro statements; the posture is attributable to his administration even when the language comes through ministers or the UN mission.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score of 6 is too high because the record remains hedged, with neutrality language, abstentions, and a questionable Moscow signal before the invasion. I did not go lower because a score of 4 is too low because Brazil did support diplomacy, humanitarian protection, and UN accountability positions on Ukraine.

evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on the immediate political effect of the legal challenge.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Bolsonaro's post-election conduct and its effects.
contrary_evidence: The article discusses potential political impact, not a direct order to protest or violence.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he had sought 'alternatives' after his election defeat but did not detail them, while Reuters reported that he had continued to question the electoral result and claimed to stay within 'the four lines of the Constitution'.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz que buscou sem sucesso 'alternativas' após derrota e que não é hora de 'tudo ou nada'
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he had sought 'alternatives' after his election defeat but did not detail them, while Reuters reported that he had continued to question the electoral result and claimed to stay within 'the four lines of the Constitution'.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report on Bolsonaro's own post-defeat explanation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution.
contrary_evidence: The statement is ambiguous and does not prove a specific illegal plan.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Bolsonaro's anti-human-rights campaign discourse and attacks on institutions helped create an intimidatory climate.
Undermining Indigenous protection, land recognition, and environmental agencies materially weakened safety for Indigenous communities.
Dozens of executive orders liberalizing firearms rules increased the risk environment rather than reducing domestic fear.
The sharp rise in gun ownership and leakage to criminal gangs shows downstream public-safety harm from that policy.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: After defeat, Bolsonaro urged supporters to unblock roads, which is a restraint signal rather than incitement to violence.
The election-result challenge was weak on the merits and described as stoking protest rather than directing violence.
The constitutional frame gave formal power, but it does not prove how far Bolsonaro could or did control state-level violence in practice.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil's federal structure and decentralized policing limited direct national control over many abuses; the score reflects Bolsonaro's policy climate and tolerance, not every local act of violence.
judge.ruler_attribution: Strong for discourse, agenda-setting, and federal policy; weaker for direct command over many state-level abuses.

contrary_evidence.explanation: He explicitly told supporters to unblock roads after the election.
The post-election challenge was more an agitation signal than a direct violence order.
Formal constitutional authority existed, but formal power alone does not show direct violence control.

judge.source_mix: Constitutional text, rights NGOs, Reuters-style reporting, and court reporting; no client matrix used.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were unavailable across the lens set, so the judgment rests entirely on the embedded evidence and contrary notes.
judge.chapter_rationale: Bolsonaro lands in the lower-middle band because the dossier shows a hostile domestic-safety climate without evidence of full-scale state terror. The strongest negative facts are his repeated attacks on institutions and journalists, the weakening of Indigenous and environmental protections, and the gun-liberalization agenda that raised downstream violence risk. The counterevidence is real but limited: he told supporters to clear road blockades and some of the post-election messaging was restraining rather than violent. That keeps the score above the severe-authoritarian floor, but far below the high-restraint band, because the record still shows recurring intimidation, weakened protections, and state-environment harms rather than durable safety gains.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: I rejected 2-3 because the record is coercive and harmful, but it does not show the kind of pervasive torture/disappearance regime required for the lower authoritarian bands.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: I rejected 6+ because the evidence is dominated by intimidation, institutional undermining, and public-safety deterioration, with only modest restraint signals.

chapter_specific.value: weak; courts and institutions resisted some abuse, but the executive climate remained hostile
strained; rhetoric, institutional attacks, and journalistic intimidation were central
worsened protection for vulnerable groups and the press, despite some post-defeat restraint
high for policy and rhetoric, moderate for downstream state violence
3B.1 and 3B.2 are weaker than the incitement, vulnerable-group, and emergency-policy lenses

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Jair Bolsonaro's record on domestic safety in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Bolsonaro's anti-human-rights campaign discourse and attacks on institutions helped create an intimidatory climate; and HRW said the Bolsonaro administration undermined the agency protecting Indigenous peoples, halted recognition of traditional lands, weakened environmental agencies, and left Indigenous territories more vulnerable to encroachment.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: After his defeat, Bolsonaro told supporters to unblock roads, saying protests were part of democracy but road blockades violated people's right to come and go; and Bolsonaro's challenge to the election result was seen by analysts as weak on the merits but capable of firing up supporters who were already protesting his loss.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Strong for discourse, agenda-setting, and federal policy; weaker for direct command over many state-level abuses.

Taken together, I did not go higher because I rejected 6+ because the evidence is dominated by intimidation, institutional undermining, and public-safety deterioration, with only modest restraint signals. I did not go lower because I rejected 2-3 because the record is coercive and harmful, but it does not show the kind of pervasive torture/disappearance regime required for the lower authoritarian bands.

evidence.claim: The TSE said Lula won the second round of the 2022 presidential election with 50.83% of valid votes against Bolsonaro's 49.17%, and that Bolsonaro was the incumbent president who had sought reelection.
evidence.title: Lula é eleito novamente presidente da República do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said Lula won the second round of the 2022 presidential election with 50.83% of valid votes against Bolsonaro's 49.17%, and that Bolsonaro was the incumbent president who had sought reelection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election authority record with official result totals.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Bolsonaro's contestability and transfer-of-power obligation.
contrary_evidence: This proves turnover occurred, but not that Bolsonaro himself accepted it promptly or in good faith.

evidence.claim: The TSE said no fraud had been documented since electronic voting began in 1996, noted that the system had elected multiple presidents including Bolsonaro, and stated that the process had permitted alternation in power.
evidence.title: Nota à imprensa
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said no fraud had been documented since electronic voting began in 1996, noted that the system had elected multiple presidents including Bolsonaro, and stated that the process had permitted alternation in power.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary court/election authority statement responding directly to Bolsonaro's fraud allegations.
evidence.period_fit: Inherited baseline relevant to the 2022 campaign and post-election dispute.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's repeated fraud narrative, though the statement itself is institutional.
contrary_evidence: It is a court rebuttal, not an independent empirical audit of every election claim.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said disinformation amplified by Bolsonaro and his allies flooded the online landscape ahead of the October 2022 election, that Bolsonaro had made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that those claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as an organized disinformation machine.
evidence.title: Brazil: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said disinformation amplified by Bolsonaro and his allies flooded the online landscape ahead of the October 2022 election, that Bolsonaro had made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that those claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as an organized disinformation machine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major independent monitoring report with detailed 2022 case coverage and attribution to Bolsonaro and allies.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Bolsonaro attribution for the statements and the political network around them.
contrary_evidence: Freedom House is an advocacy/monitoring source and may emphasize harms more than institutional defenses.

evidence.claim: The TSE said the authenticity test proved the official election-system software was installed in the electronic voting machines and that the test was public, real-time, and conducted before voting began.
evidence.title: Justiça Eleitoral realiza Teste de Autenticidade dos Sistemas Eleitorais antes da votação
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said the authenticity test proved the official election-system software was installed in the electronic voting machines and that the test was public, real-time, and conducted before voting began.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election-authority description of the audit procedure in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional counterweight to Bolsonaro's fraud narrative rather than a Bolsonaro action.
contrary_evidence: This demonstrates institutional resilience, not Bolsonaro's own commitment to that resilience.

evidence.claim: The TSE said the first round of the 2022 election and the days after it were marked by intense proliferation of fake news about the electoral process, and that the court and partner fact-checkers debunked the main false claims.
evidence.title: Fato ou Boato: Justiça Eleitoral desmentiu as principais fake news sobre o processo eleitoral em 2022
evidence.excerpt: The TSE said the first round of the 2022 election and the days after it were marked by intense proliferation of fake news about the electoral process, and that the court and partner fact-checkers debunked the main false claims.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary election-authority article directly describing the 2022 misinformation wave and its rebuttal.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The misinformation environment is Bolsonaro-linked, though the article itself is about election administration response.
contrary_evidence: This is institutional-response evidence, not direct evidence of Bolsonaro personally authoring each falsehood.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The election authority's result confirms a competitive election and an actual transfer-of-power outcome rather than a closed-authoritarian entrenchment.
The TSE's authenticity test and public voting safeguards support a still-functioning electoral system despite Bolsonaro's fraud narrative.
The TSE's post-election rebuttal of fake news shows institutional resistance to Bolsonaro-linked disinformation, which kept contestability alive.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Freedom House describes Bolsonaro and allies flooding the campaign with disinformation, which materially degraded the information environment.
The TSE's prior rebuttal to Bolsonaro's fraud claims is relevant as context for his repeated attacks on electoral legitimacy, though the institution held.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil entered 2022 with competitive elections and resilient institutions, and Bolsonaro governed within a system that still forced a real transfer outcome. His conduct degraded the information environment, but he did not successfully break the electoral framework.
judge.ruler_attribution: Mixed but meaningful: the evidence links Bolsonaro directly to fraud rhetoric and disinformation, but many countervailing facts are institutional rather than personal.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The election result and turnover undercut any claim that Bolsonaro successfully closed the system.
Institutional audit procedures remained public and operational, which limits the score from falling into the authoritarian range.

judge.source_mix: Primary election-authority records plus Freedom House and Reuters-based reporting. The strongest evidence is institutional and official, while the main negative evidence is Bolsonaro-linked disinformation and fraud rhetoric.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment; the judge relied entirely on the embedded projection and its cited evidence.
judge.chapter_rationale: Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 record is mixed and clearly erosive, but not successfully authoritarian. He helped poison the information environment with disinformation and fraud claims, and he did so against a backdrop of repeated institutional conflict with the election system. However, Brazil still held a competitive election, the election authority publicly audited the process, and power actually transferred after Bolsonaro lost. That combination keeps the score above the genuinely backsliding or semi-closed regimes, but below the high-trust democratic anchors. The evidence supports a middling score because Bolsonaro weakened contestability without extinguishing it.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the fact that the election still produced an opposition victory and that electoral institutions held up under pressure.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would overstate restraint. Bolsonaro repeatedly attacked electoral legitimacy and amplified disinformation, which materially damaged political freedom even though institutions survived.

chapter_specific.value: Mixed and erosive: democratic turnover survived, but Bolsonaro's disinformation campaign and legitimacy attacks weakened confidence in contestability.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Jair Bolsonaro's record on political freedom in 2022 was assessed as generally positive, with important limitations, resulting in a score of 6 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The TSE said Lula won the second round of the 2022 presidential election with 50.83% of valid votes against Bolsonaro's 49.17%, and that Bolsonaro was the incumbent president who had sought reelection; and The TSE said the authenticity test proved the official election-system software was installed in the electronic voting machines and that the test was public, real-time, and conducted before voting began.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Freedom House said disinformation amplified by Bolsonaro and his allies flooded the online landscape ahead of the October 2022 election, that Bolsonaro had made at least 6,000 false or misleading statements by August 2022, and that those claims were reproduced through official channels and social media as an organized disinformation machine; and The TSE said no fraud had been documented since electronic voting began in 1996, noted that the system had elected multiple presidents including Bolsonaro, and stated that the process had permitted alternation in power.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed but meaningful: the evidence links Bolsonaro directly to fraud rhetoric and disinformation, but many countervailing facts are institutional rather than personal.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would overstate restraint. Bolsonaro repeatedly attacked electoral legitimacy and amplified disinformation, which materially damaged political freedom even though institutions survived. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the fact that the election still produced an opposition victory and that electoral institutions held up under pressure.

evidence.claim: Brazil's GDP grew 2.9% in 2022, with services up 4.2%, industry up 1.6%, and agriculture down 1.7%.
evidence.title: GDP grows 2.9% in 2022, closes the year at R$9.9 trillion
evidence.excerpt: Brazil's GDP grew 2.9% in 2022, with services up 4.2%, industry up 1.6%, and agriculture down 1.7%.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IBGE is the official national statistics agency and this is a standard GDP release with direct annual estimates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 target year; published March 2023 with the final annual estimate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual, not uniquely attributable to Bolsonaro; reflects the full-year macro record under his administration plus global and domestic conditions.
contrary_evidence: Growth remained uneven across sectors.
Does not by itself show ruler-driven prosperity gains.

evidence.claim: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022.
evidence.title: Inflação de alimentos e insegurança alimentar no Brasil
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022.
evidence.source_locator: Body text discussing 2022 food insecurity and prices
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank analysis is high-quality and explicitly links 2022 food insecurity to inflation and household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Explicitly discusses 2022 conditions, with retrospective comparisons to 2019-2021.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly contextual, but relevant to policy because social protection and inflation responses during Bolsonaro's term affected household exposure.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes social-protection measures cushioned the worst pandemic-era losses.
The evidence does not isolate Bolsonaro from inherited pandemic effects.

evidence.claim: By mid-2022, annual inflation in Brazil was estimated at 13.9%, and food costs had risen 13.43% in the 12 months to August 2022.
evidence.title: Fighting against poverty: the impact of inflation on households’ purchasing power
evidence.excerpt: By mid-2022, annual inflation in Brazil was estimated at 13.9%, and food costs had risen 13.43% in the 12 months to August 2022.
evidence.source_locator: Opinion text / data paragraph on Brazil
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank staff commentary draws on contemporaneous price data and is directly tied to household welfare.
evidence.period_fit: Directly addresses 2022 price conditions, published in October 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual; reflects inflation that Bolsonaro's government tried to offset but did not fully control.
contrary_evidence: Nominal average labor incomes also rose, partly offsetting the shock.
The piece is analytic commentary, not a ruler-specific audit.

evidence.claim: Copom said Brazilian activity was growing above expectations and the labor market was recovering, but inflation remained high and broad-based, with food and fuel shocks still prominent.
evidence.title: Atas do Comitê de Política Monetária - Copom
evidence.excerpt: Copom said Brazilian activity was growing above expectations and the labor market was recovering, but inflation remained high and broad-based, with food and fuel shocks still prominent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank minutes documenting the state of the 2022 economy and inflation drivers.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual rather than directly attributable to Bolsonaro, but relevant to the administration's economic environment and response choices.
contrary_evidence: The central bank attributes some weakness to global and commodity shocks.
Positive output and labor recovery complicate any one-direction verdict.

evidence.claim: Copom said the labor market continued to recover, consumer inflation had recently been reduced by tax measures and lower fuel prices, but underlying inflation remained above the range compatible with the inflation target.
evidence.title: Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee — Copom
evidence.excerpt: Copom said the labor market continued to recover, consumer inflation had recently been reduced by tax measures and lower fuel prices, but underlying inflation remained above the range compatible with the inflation target.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the primary monetary-policy record for October 2022 and directly documents the inflation dynamic.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual; the tax measures were part of the Bolsonaro government's policy mix, while monetary policy was independent.
contrary_evidence: Tax-driven disinflation can be temporary and fiscally costly.
Underlying inflation still remained elevated.

evidence.claim: Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.title: Brazil Congress approves major spending bill, lifting Bolsonaro re-election hopes
evidence.excerpt: Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is strong independent coverage, though the piece relies partly on market expectations and political context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct enough to Bolsonaro's reelection strategy because the package was explicitly tied to his campaign and administration.
contrary_evidence: Government said it needed urgent relief for households hit by inflation.
The package had congressional approval, not sole presidential unilateral action.

evidence.claim: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.title: SAIBA MAIS-Benefícios em série e promessas de Bolsonaro em ano eleitoral têm custo de R$273 bi em 2022 e 2023
evidence.excerpt: Reuters estimated that Bolsonaro's 2022 election-year benefits and promises would cost R$273 billion in 2022-2023, with R$127.4 billion already approved and implemented.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent source, and the UOL mirror preserves the original report and numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the election period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's election strategy and executive choices.
contrary_evidence: Some measures were already approved through Congress, not by executive fiat alone.
Short-term relief can be justified in inflationary periods, but fiscal sustainability is the counterpoint.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro said he expected deflation the following month because lower fuel prices after an ICMS tax change would reduce inflation.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro diz esperar deflação em agosto com queda no preço dos combustíveis
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro said he expected deflation the following month because lower fuel prices after an ICMS tax change would reduce inflation.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters captured the president's own public statement, which is reliable for the claim he made even if not for its predictive accuracy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential rhetoric and policy framing.
contrary_evidence: The effect was framed as temporary and dependent on tax changes.
Fuel-tax relief can also be fiscally costly and not structurally anti-inflationary.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro acknowledged inflation in food and fuel but blamed state governors and the war in Ukraine for the price surge.
evidence.title: Bolsonaro reconhece inflação, mas culpa estados e guerra na Ucrânia
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro acknowledged inflation in food and fuel but blamed state governors and the war in Ukraine for the price surge.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted remarks in the Reuters report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is reliable for contemporaneous public statements and the piece directly captures Bolsonaro's rhetoric.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential rhetoric, relevant to honesty and accountability for shocks.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine war and global commodity shocks were real external drivers.
The statement alone does not prove policy failure or success.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro issued a decree delegating to the Economy Minister authority over opening 2022 budget credits and related budget adjustments to speed execution.
evidence.title: Decreto prevê delegação de competências ao Ministro de Estado da Economia
evidence.publisher: Secretaria-Geral da Presidência / Governo do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro issued a decree delegating to the Economy Minister authority over opening 2022 budget credits and related budget adjustments to speed execution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the official government announcement of an enacted decree with a clear administrative delegation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct and strong: this was a presidential decree under Bolsonaro's authority.
contrary_evidence: Delegation does not prove the minister was competent, only that he was empowered.
Budget execution still faced fiscal and inflationary constraints.

evidence.claim: Bolsonaro signed a law extending payroll-tax relief through 2023 for 17 labor-intensive sectors, including construction, transport, and communications.
evidence.title: Presidente Bolsonaro sanciona Projeto de Lei da desoneração da folha de pagamento de 17 setores da economia
evidence.publisher: Secretaria-Geral da Presidência / Governo do Brasil
evidence.excerpt: Bolsonaro signed a law extending payroll-tax relief through 2023 for 17 labor-intensive sectors, including construction, transport, and communications.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official record of the enacted measure and its stated policy purpose.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022, though the law was signed at the start of the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action, though the measure originated in Congress and was framed as a jobs policy.
contrary_evidence: Sectoral tax relief can privilege connected industries rather than broad-based reform.
The measure creates revenue costs that have to be offset elsewhere.

evidence.claim: The government said the Investment Partnership Program would invest BRL 78 billion in 2022 and that commitments signed between 2019 and 2022 would exceed BRL 1.3 trillion over coming years.
evidence.title: Brazil's investments will exceed BRL 1.3 trillion in the coming years
evidence.excerpt: The government said the Investment Partnership Program would invest BRL 78 billion in 2022 and that commitments signed between 2019 and 2022 would exceed BRL 1.3 trillion over coming years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program summary is reliable for what the administration claimed and what commitments it reported, though not all downstream effects are independently verified here.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Bolsonaro's administration and its investment policy agenda.
contrary_evidence: This is a pipeline/commitment figure, not a measured welfare outcome.
Long-run effectiveness depends on execution and project quality.

evidence.claim: The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.
evidence.title: Secretaria Especial do PPI concluiu 48 projetos em 2022 e assegurou R$ 101 bilhões em novos investimentos
evidence.excerpt: The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official year-end program report on completed projects and contracted investment, with clear implementation language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's investment-policy execution, though project-level economics depend on private actors and regulators.
contrary_evidence: Contracted investments are not the same as realized household welfare gains.
Infrastructure gains are long run and uneven.

evidence.claim: The government said Plano Safra 2022/23 would provide R$340.88 billion in rural credit, up 36% from the previous plan.
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock / Government of Brazil
evidence.excerpt: The government said Plano Safra 2022/23 would provide R$340.88 billion in rural credit, up 36% from the previous plan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is the official launch page for the 2022/23 rural credit program, with the stated amount and percentage increase.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct government policy under Bolsonaro, though sectoral benefits are concentrated in agriculture rather than the whole economy.
contrary_evidence: Sectoral credit expansion can help productivity but does not prove broad household welfare gains.
Agricultural output can also be exposed to commodity and weather cycles.

evidence.claim: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection.
evidence.title: Governo Federal apresenta superávit primário de R$ 59,7 bilhões em 2022
evidence.excerpt: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: National Treasury is the authoritative source for the official fiscal outcome and the release gives the final figure directly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the Bolsonaro administration's fiscal choices, but the result also reflects one-offs, transfers, and revenue conditions beyond his control.
contrary_evidence: A surplus does not erase election-year spending expansion or inflation pressure.
The headline result may not reflect underlying sustainability or quality of spending.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The 2022 primary surplus suggests fiscal outcomes were not uniformly poor.
Investment and contracted-project activity show some state-capacity and infrastructure follow-through.
GDP growth remained positive in 2022 despite the difficult environment.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Food insecurity and food-price pressure were severe and broadly felt.
Election-year spending that bypassed the cap raised fiscal and inflation concerns.
Inflation stayed elevated and household purchasing power remained under strain.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil entered 2022 with post-pandemic recovery, inflation shocks, and labor-market weakness; global commodity and food-price swings mattered a lot, but so did election-year fiscal choices.
judge.ruler_attribution: Attribution is mixed: some positive growth and fiscal outcomes reflect the broader recovery and institutional settings, while the most salient negative choices were clearly linked to Bolsonaro's political strategy.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Positive GDP growth kept the score from dropping further.
A primary surplus and completed projects provide some counterweight.

judge.source_mix: Official statistics, central-bank minutes, World Bank analysis, Reuters reporting, and government program releases; no structured local priors were collected in this experiment.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were unavailable across all lenses, so the judge relied on the embedded dossier evidence and the source-confidence framing only.
judge.chapter_rationale: Bolsonaro lands at 4.5 because the year mixed real macro activity with clearly harmful short-term politics and weak household outcomes. Growth, employment, investment, and even a fiscal surplus show that the economy was not collapsing, but food insecurity, inflation, and election-year spending that strained fiscal credibility kept the chapter firmly below the competence threshold. The evidence supports a mixed record with some competent outcomes, yet not enough fairness, durability, or restraint to justify a higher score.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score near 3 would ignore the positive growth, surplus, and investment evidence.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score near 6 would overstate the policy quality because food insecurity, inflation, and fiscal loosening were serious and ruler-linked.

chapter_specific.value: Mixed and uneven: output and employment improved, but inflation, food insecurity, and election-year fiscal loosening eroded the prosperity story.
Commodity and food-price shocks mattered, but the administration amplified them through discretionary spending and weak structural reform.
Household welfare lagged headline growth; the food-insecurity evidence is the clearest sign that gains were not broadly shared.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Jair Bolsonaro's record on economic well-being in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The federal government reported a 2022 primary surplus of R$59.7 billion, above the year's formal projection; and The PPI said it concluded 48 projects in 2022 and secured more than R$101 billion in contracted investments, including the Eletrobras capitalisation and airport concessions.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and said food prices rose 37.5% between end-2019 and end-2022; and Congress approved a spending package Bolsonaro was banking on for reelection that bypassed the spending cap and boosted social benefits, prompting investor concern about fiscal discipline and inflation.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Attribution is mixed: some positive growth and fiscal outcomes reflect the broader recovery and institutional settings, while the most salient negative choices were clearly linked to Bolsonaro's political strategy.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score near 6 would overstate the policy quality because food insecurity, inflation, and fiscal loosening were serious and ruler-linked. I did not go lower because a score near 3 would ignore the positive growth, surplus, and investment evidence.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Auxílio Brasil conditionalities were tied to health and education tracking, showing concrete welfare administration.
Targeting updates for social assistance show some capacity to improve program administration.
Internet Brasil and related connectivity policy added real education access support.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Millions of children and adolescents were out of school, which signals a serious human-development problem.
Food insecurity and poverty remained very high in 2022 despite some cushioning from transfers.
Program monitoring problems led to sanctions being annulled, showing weak execution quality.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Brazil in 2022 had pandemic aftershocks, inflation, and deep structural inequality. Bolsonaro can claim some targeted welfare action, but the baseline was poor and the year still ended with large child poverty, food insecurity, and school exclusion.
judge.ruler_attribution: The strongest evidence is government-level and programmatic rather than personal; Bolsonaro is tied to the policy environment and executive choices, but many outcomes reflect pandemic, Congress, and subnational conditions.

contrary_evidence.explanation: School non-attendance and child labor remain major welfare failures.
Food insecurity and poverty show the welfare picture was still badly compromised.

judge.source_mix: Official Brazilian sources and Reuters/UNICEF/World Bank corroboration, with an overall evidence picture that mixes program design, implementation fixes, and negative household indicators.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment, so the judgment relies on the embedded dossier evidence, the reviewer exclusions already present there, and cross-case calibration within the batch.
judge.chapter_rationale: Bolsonaro receives a mixed score because the dossier contains real social-policy machinery, especially around conditional transfers, connectivity, and administrative targeting. But the year still shows deep welfare weakness: child poverty, school exclusion, food insecurity, and monitoring failures remain severe, and the most positive evidence is often about process rather than durable outcomes. The score sits below the middle only modestly because the government did do more than posture; it simply did not convert that into broad, reliable human-development gains.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would miss the fact that the administration did deploy real welfare programs and administrative corrections in 2022.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require stronger evidence of broad, durable reductions in poverty and exclusion, which the dossier does not provide.

chapter_specific.value: education, social protection, connectivity, housing, child welfare
some vulnerable groups were explicitly targeted, but exclusion and school non-attendance remained large
inflation and pandemic aftershocks shaped the welfare record
mixed: real policy action, but weak and uneven human-development outcomes

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Jair Bolsonaro's record on social well-being in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The decree assigns health and education ministries responsibility for tracking Auxílio Brasil conditionalities, requires information sharing with the Ministry of Citizenship, and provides for social-assistance priority and review when families miss conditions; and The government said Auxílio Brasil updated periodic data-verification rules to improve targeting by identifying discrepancies in family records against other federal databases.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: UNICEF said 2 million children and adolescents aged 11 to 19 were not attending school in Brazil, equal to 11% of the survey sample, and linked the problem to child labor and learning difficulties; and The World Bank estimated that 30.7% of Brazil's population experienced moderate or severe food insecurity in 2022, and projected poverty at about 24.3% for 2022 as labor-market recovery and Bolsa Família adjustments offset some losses.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: The strongest evidence is government-level and programmatic rather than personal; Bolsonaro is tied to the policy environment and executive choices, but many outcomes reflect pandemic, Congress, and subnational conditions.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would require stronger evidence of broad, durable reductions in poverty and exclusion, which the dossier does not provide. I did not go lower because a lower score would miss the fact that the administration did deploy real welfare programs and administrative corrections in 2022.
