judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Mexico entered 2022 with substantial social-program capacity and a severe legacy of inequality and health-system weakness. That allows real credit for targeted transfers and federalization efforts, but it also means the score must remain tempered by persistent access problems.
judge.ruler_attribution: AMLO is directly associated with the welfare architecture and public claims, but many gains are shared with ministries, states, and preexisting structural trends. The dossier supports meaningful president-level responsibility, not exclusive personal causation.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Deteriorating access to health is a serious counterweight to the positive program rollout.
Some of the most positive figures are long-run continuation of earlier social architecture rather than unique 2022 change.

judge.source_mix: Mostly official Mexican government material plus World Bank and independent research summaries. The dossier is strong on scale and delivery, weaker on clean causal separation and independent outcome audits.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment, so the judgment relies on the embedded dossier evidence, the reviewer exclusions already present there, and cross-case calibration within the batch.
judge.chapter_rationale: López Obrador receives a moderately strong score because the 2022 record shows real welfare delivery at scale: health federalization, education budgets, disability pensions, direct transfers, and disaster-linked relief all reached large numbers of people. The score is capped because health access deteriorated and because not all positive movement can be cleanly separated from earlier reforms or broader labor-market change. This is a substantive welfare state in motion, but not a cleanly documented, fully consolidated human-development breakthrough.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would fail to credit the breadth and scale of welfare delivery documented in the dossier.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would require stronger evidence that 2022 welfare gains were more durable, more equitable, and more clearly attributable to AMLO's direct actions.

chapter_specific.value: health, education, pensions, disaster relief, food/consumption support
poor households, indigenous and afromexican communities, disabled people, and disaster victims are explicitly targeted
post-pandemic recovery and inflation are central to the welfare story
substantial expansion in coverage, but health access and quality remain a concern

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Andrés Manuel López Obrador's record on social well-being in 2022 was assessed as generally positive, with important limitations, resulting in a score of 6.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The federal government issued a mandatory Program Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar that aims to guarantee progressive, free, integral health services for people without social security and to strengthen federalization of health services; and IMSS-Bienestar expansion and staffing show real federal health delivery under the administration.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: BBVA Research summarized Coneval's 2022 measurement, saying 46.8 million people were in poverty and 9.1 million in extreme poverty, while access to health worsened between 2018 and 2022; and Poverty reduction is real but mainly driven by labor-market effects and not a complete welfare settlement.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: AMLO is directly associated with the welfare architecture and public claims, but many gains are shared with ministries, states, and preexisting structural trends. The dossier supports meaningful president-level responsibility, not exclusive personal causation.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would require stronger evidence that 2022 welfare gains were more durable, more equitable, and more clearly attributable to AMLO's direct actions. I did not go lower because a lower score would fail to credit the breadth and scale of welfare delivery documented in the dossier.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.
evidence.title: 16.11.22 Versión estenográfica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the accusation that the reform sought his reelection was false and that the reform did not propose presidential reelection.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct ruler statement in an official transcript, but embedded in a partisan information campaign.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement about transfer rules and succession.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public position.
contrary_evidence: The same transcript also promotes a broad electoral overhaul that critics said would weaken independent institutions.
Self-denial is not independent proof of future compliance.

evidence.claim: AMLO's daily morning briefings became more aggressive toward journalists; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment naming journalists and outlets he said published false stories, and he divides media into 'good' and 'bad' camps.
evidence.title: México
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: AMLO's daily morning briefings became more aggressive toward journalists; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment naming journalists and outlets he said published false stories, and he divides media into 'good' and 'bad' camps.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: University-based journalism research center; contemporaneous country report with clear description of AMLO's repeated public behavior.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers the 2022 Mexico media environment during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public communication style; it does not by itself prove falsehood on any single story, but it does show his chosen rhetoric and targeting of critics.
contrary_evidence: Mexico still had active independent media and public criticism; the report is descriptive and does not adjudicate specific accusations.

evidence.claim: AMLO publicly revealed the alleged salary of Carlos Loret de Mola, a journalist who had reported on his family, and the article says many believed the details were illegally acquired from tax authorities.
evidence.title: Mexican president lashes out at EU 'lies' over his media-bashing rhetoric
evidence.excerpt: AMLO publicly revealed the alleged salary of Carlos Loret de Mola, a journalist who had reported on his family, and the article says many believed the details were illegally acquired from tax authorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable international newspaper citing contemporaneous reporting and direct political reaction; the tax-leak implication is reported rather than independently proven in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's response to criticism; the underlying salary data leak is not independently adjudicated here.
contrary_evidence: The article does not prove the tax-authority leak; it reports suspicion and criticism from observers.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the investigation into his son's alleged conflict of interest was open, asked who owned the Houston house and what Pemex contracts were involved, but also said investigators would find nothing and later attacked the reporter who broke the story.
evidence.title: López Obrador dice que está 'abierta la investigación' contra su hijo
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the investigation into his son's alleged conflict of interest was open, asked who owned the Houston house and what Pemex contracts were involved, but also said investigators would find nothing and later attacked the reporter who broke the story.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Wire-based report with direct quotations from AMLO and the surrounding controversy; the underlying allegations remained unproven in the article.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's public response to allegations involving his son and a contractor-linked house.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish wrongdoing; it records allegations, AMLO's denial, and a call for formal investigation.

evidence.claim: The European Parliament said Mexican authorities had shown systematic criticism and intimidation of journalists, cited clear signs of Pegasus use against journalists and rights defenders, and warned that AMLO-era electoral and judicial reforms raised rule-of-law concerns.
evidence.title: Mexico: The EP calls for the protection of journalists and activists to be guaranteed
evidence.excerpt: The European Parliament said Mexican authorities had shown systematic criticism and intimidation of journalists, cited clear signs of Pegasus use against journalists and rights defenders, and warned that AMLO-era electoral and judicial reforms raised rule-of-law concerns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Formal parliamentary resolution by a major external institution, contemporaneous with the target year, with specific findings and concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Targets the AMLO administration and its rhetoric/policies; it does not itself prove personal criminal intent, but it is directly relevant to ruler-level tolerance and use of power.
contrary_evidence: A parliamentary resolution is political monitoring, not a court judgment; it does not conclusively establish personal wrongdoing by AMLO.

evidence.claim: AMLO said his electoral reform would guarantee clean and free elections, leave behind electoral fraud, and prevent any government, company, or economic power from buying votes.
evidence.title: Presidente presenta iniciativa de reforma electoral; incluye creacion del INEC y reduccion de gasto a partidos politicos
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said his electoral reform would guarantee clean and free elections, leave behind electoral fraud, and prevent any government, company, or economic power from buying votes.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and quoted reform justification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement; useful for stated intent, but self-serving and not proof of effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's stated commitment, but the claim is about intent rather than verified effect.
contrary_evidence: Later reporting and opposition criticism argued the reform could weaken electoral independence.

evidence.claim: AMLO described the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment as a summary of media lies and social-media manipulation, and framed critical media coverage as false.
evidence.title: 07.09.22 Version estenografica de la conferencia de prensa matutina del presidente Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador
evidence.excerpt: AMLO described the 'Who's Who in Lies' segment as a summary of media lies and social-media manipulation, and framed critical media coverage as false.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary transcript of AMLO's own words and the official framing of the government segment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own public communication strategy.
contrary_evidence: An official fact-checking segment can be legitimate in principle, but the phrasing here is overtly stigmatizing and not neutral.

evidence.claim: The SFP issued an 'Acuerdo de Conclusion por Falta de Elementos' and reported no evidence supporting conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno involving AMLO, his son, and Daniel Chavez in the 'Casa Gris' matter.
evidence.title: La SFP exonera a AMLO, su hijo y Daniel Chavez de conflicto de interes
evidence.excerpt: The SFP issued an 'Acuerdo de Conclusion por Falta de Elementos' and reported no evidence supporting conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno involving AMLO, his son, and Daniel Chavez in the 'Casa Gris' matter.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Credible Mexican business-political reporting on an official administrative finding; the underlying finding is relevant but limited by jurisdiction and evidentiary scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to AMLO because the case touched his family and his administration's conflict-of-interest review; the finding is about absence of evidence, not proof of innocence.
contrary_evidence: The article itself notes criticism that the SFP lacked evidence and that its jurisdiction did not cover foreign transactions or acts outside the federal administration.

evidence.claim: The article says AMLO was seeking a Banxico successor more aligned with his political vision and that government job offers were being used as pressure as Gerardo Esquivel's term neared expiry.
evidence.title: Gerardo Esquivel rechaza ofertas laborales del Gobierno de Mexico
evidence.excerpt: The article says AMLO was seeking a Banxico successor more aligned with his political vision and that government job offers were being used as pressure as Gerardo Esquivel's term neared expiry.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Financial-news reporting based on unnamed sources; plausible and specific, but not fully documentary.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's personnel preferences and the government's approach to Banxico appointments, though the sourcing is indirect.
contrary_evidence: Esquivel had earlier been an AMLO adviser and the article does not prove self-dealing or corruption; it is about alignment and institutional independence.

evidence.claim: AMLO withdrew his previous Banxico nominee and selected Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, a public-finance official with strong budget experience but little monetary-policy experience, prompting concerns about politicization of the central bank.
evidence.title: Factbox-Victoria Rodriguez, Mexico's new pick for central bank governor
evidence.excerpt: AMLO withdrew his previous Banxico nominee and selected Victoria Rodriguez Ceja, a public-finance official with strong budget experience but little monetary-policy experience, prompting concerns about politicization of the central bank.
evidence.source_locator: factbox bullet list and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox based on contemporaneous reporting and biographical detail; the loyalty concern is inferential but clearly stated by the article.
evidence.period_fit: Late-2021 nomination with a 2022 start date and 2022 consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's nomination choice; the competence-versus-loyalty inference is based on the article's framing and market reaction.
contrary_evidence: The same article notes Rodriguez had extensive public-finance experience and formal economics training.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The 'Who's Who in Lies' framing shows a sustained antagonistic posture toward journalists and a willingness to stigmatize critics.
Publicly revealing a journalist's salary after the journalist had reported on his family raises a direct retaliation concern.
AMLO's response to the investigation into his son's alleged conflict of interest is direct, personal, and heavily defensive.
The European Parliament resolution adds an external integrity signal about intimidation and Pegasus-related concerns under the administration.
The Casa Gris administrative finding does not prove innocence in every sense, but it narrows one major allegation and keeps the score from dropping further.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The electoral-reform rhetoric is a direct public commitment that complicates any pure authoritarian reading.
The SFP no-evidence finding is a meaningful mitigation, even if it is limited in scope.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: No structured local priors were collected. Mexico's open conflict over media and corruption is context only; the score turns on AMLO's own statements, journalistic targeting, and the family-linked allegations in the dossier.
judge.ruler_attribution: Direct on repeated public rhetoric and family-linked controversy, but weak on final adjudication of the deeper allegations. The file shows hostile treatment of critics and defensive messaging more than proven private enrichment.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The electoral reform pitch shows an anti-fraud public narrative, even if it is self-serving.
One administrative finding found no supporting evidence for the Casa Gris conflict allegation.

judge.source_mix: Official transcripts, investigative journalism, a parliamentary resolution, and an administrative finding. Strongest on rhetoric and scrutiny; weaker where the allegations remain disputed or only partially substantiated.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Local priors unavailable in this experiment; judgment depends only on the dossier evidence.
judge.chapter_rationale: AMLO scores low because the dossier contains repeated hostile and misleading rhetoric toward journalists, a retaliatory disclosure of a reporter's salary, and family-linked allegations that he answered in a deeply defensive way. The cleanest mitigation is one administrative finding that found no evidence in the Casa Gris matter, plus his own reform rhetoric. Those are real but limited counterweights. The file therefore supports a score below the middle for recurring combative behavior and selective honesty, but not a full collapse into the bottom tier.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score below 3 would overstate the degree to which the available allegations were actually proven. One administrative finding and some reform rhetoric matter here.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score above 4 would underweight the repeated stigmatizing media posture and the direct family-linked controversies. The pattern is not clean.
judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Andrés Manuel López Obrador's record on integrity in 2022 was assessed as poor, resulting in a score of 3.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: AMLO's daily morning briefings became more aggressive toward journalists; in July 2021 he added a 'Who's Who' segment naming journalists and outlets he said published false stories, and he divides media into 'good' and 'bad' camps; and AMLO publicly revealed the alleged salary of Carlos Loret de Mola, a journalist who had reported on his family, and the article says many believed the details were illegally acquired from tax authorities.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: AMLO said his electoral reform would guarantee clean and free elections, leave behind electoral fraud, and prevent any government, company, or economic power from buying votes; and The SFP issued an 'Acuerdo de Conclusion por Falta de Elementos' and reported no evidence supporting conflict of interest, cohecho, or soborno involving AMLO, his son, and Daniel Chavez in the 'Casa Gris' matter.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Direct on repeated public rhetoric and family-linked controversy, but weak on final adjudication of the deeper allegations. The file shows hostile treatment of critics and defensive messaging more than proven private enrichment.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score above 4 would underweight the repeated stigmatizing media posture and the direct family-linked controversies. The pattern is not clean. I did not go lower because a score below 3 would overstate the degree to which the available allegations were actually proven. One administrative finding and some reform rhetoric matter here.

evidence.claim: The federal government issued a mandatory Program Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar that aims to guarantee progressive, free, integral health services for people without social security and to strengthen federalization of health services.
evidence.title: ACUERDO por el que se emite el Programa Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar
evidence.publisher: Diario Oficial de la Federación / Secretaría de Salud
evidence.excerpt: The federal government issued a mandatory Program Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar that aims to guarantee progressive, free, integral health services for people without social security and to strengthen federalization of health services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official legal instrument with explicit obligations, coverage aims, and federalization language.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 policy design and implementation framework.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's government through the federal health secretariat and the national plan it cites.
contrary_evidence: This is a program order, not proof of achieved outcomes.
It does not by itself show service quality or equal access across regions.

evidence.claim: AMLO said 25 million families would receive direct benefits in 2022, equal to about 70 percent of Mexican families, and that the poorest states were already being covered at 100 percent of households.
evidence.title: El 70% de las familias son beneficiarias de al menos uno de los Programas para el Bienestar
evidence.publisher: Programas para el Bienestar / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said 25 million families would receive direct benefits in 2022, equal to about 70 percent of Mexican families, and that the poorest states were already being covered at 100 percent of households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential remarks published on the government welfare portal with specific coverage claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO, who publicly presented the distribution and coverage claims.
contrary_evidence: The claims are self-reported and do not prove outcomes or absence of exclusion.
Universal coverage in poor states is not the same as equal quality or adequacy of support.

evidence.claim: Mexico launched Bienpesca 2022 with more than 1,360 million pesos to benefit 189,000 fishers and aquaculture workers, paying each beneficiary 7,200 pesos directly and without intermediaries.
evidence.title: Gobierno de México inicia la entrega de apoyos Bienpesca 2022
evidence.publisher: Programas para el Bienestar / Gobierno de México
evidence.excerpt: Mexico launched Bienpesca 2022 with more than 1,360 million pesos to benefit 189,000 fishers and aquaculture workers, paying each beneficiary 7,200 pesos directly and without intermediaries.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government welfare portal with explicit budget, beneficiary, and anti-intermediary language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's government because the program is presented as a federal welfare policy under his administration.
contrary_evidence: This is a sector-specific transfer program, not a broad social-service overhaul.
The source is self-reported and does not test impacts on living standards.

evidence.claim: AMLO framed the 4T as a government focused on welfare for the whole population, especially the neediest, and said governability and peace remained priorities.
evidence.title: Gobierno de México garantiza bienestar y gobernabilidad, afirma presidente en 4° aniversario del triunfo de la 4T en elecciones
evidence.excerpt: AMLO framed the 4T as a government focused on welfare for the whole population, especially the neediest, and said governability and peace remained priorities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript; strong for stated program and revealed priorities, though self-presenting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own articulated program.
contrary_evidence: It states intent and self-description, not verified implementation or impact.

evidence.claim: The 2022 budget package was designed around social welfare, regional projects, and fiscal stability, with higher programmed spending for social protection, investment, health, education, and more stable debt.
evidence.title: Comunicado No. 052 Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público entrega Paquete Económico 2022 al Congreso
evidence.publisher: Secretaría de Hacienda y Crédito Público
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 budget package was designed around social welfare, regional projects, and fiscal stability, with higher programmed spending for social protection, investment, health, education, and more stable debt.
evidence.source_locator: bullet list under 'tres pilares' and spending paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget document from the finance ministry; strong for declared priorities and resource allocation.
evidence.period_fit: It sets the 2022 policy framework and funding priorities used during the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's administration through the federal budget process.
contrary_evidence: It is a plan and allocation statement, not proof that all spending translated into effective delivery.

evidence.claim: The SEP said 2022 education programs received higher budgets, including a 13.7% increase for La Escuela es Nuestra, a 4% increase for Benito Juárez scholarships, and more funding for special education.
evidence.title: Boletín SEP no. 24 Reciben programas educativos incremento presupuestal para 2022: Delfina Gómez Álvarez
evidence.excerpt: The SEP said 2022 education programs received higher budgets, including a 13.7% increase for La Escuela es Nuestra, a 4% increase for Benito Juárez scholarships, and more funding for special education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary education-ministry budget announcement with concrete program-level funding changes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's budgetary priorities and education implementation.
contrary_evidence: Budget increases do not by themselves prove learning or equity gains.

evidence.claim: La Escuela es Nuestra delivered funds directly to school parent committees, which decide use for construction, maintenance, equipment, longer hours, or student feeding.
evidence.title: Comunicado de prensa 003/2022 Madres y padres de familia son quienes deciden el uso de los recursos de La Escuela es Nuestra
evidence.excerpt: La Escuela es Nuestra delivered funds directly to school parent committees, which decide use for construction, maintenance, equipment, longer hours, or student feeding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary program rule announcement with clear delivery mechanism and local implementation design.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's delivery model for education spending.
contrary_evidence: Direct community control can improve reach, but the source itself does not measure outcomes.

evidence.claim: AMLO said the AIFA opened on time and within the original budget, presenting it as a major infrastructure delivery achieved despite legal, technical, pandemic, and supply-chain constraints.
evidence.title: 21.03.22 Versión estenográfica. Recepción e inicio de operaciones del Aeropuerto Internacional Felipe Ángeles
evidence.excerpt: AMLO said the AIFA opened on time and within the original budget, presenting it as a major infrastructure delivery achieved despite legal, technical, pandemic, and supply-chain constraints.
evidence.source_locator: central opening paragraphs on budget, timing, and construction progress
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential transcript documenting the launch and the administration's own delivery claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's own infrastructure program and the government's execution claim.
contrary_evidence: The source is self-reporting and does not by itself establish demand or operational success after opening.

evidence.claim: AMLO's plan to increase state control of power generation was defeated in parliament after opposition parties argued it would hurt investment and breach international obligations.
evidence.title: Mexican president's contentious electricity overhaul defeated in Congress
evidence.excerpt: AMLO's plan to increase state control of power generation was defeated in parliament after opposition parties argued it would hurt investment and breach international obligations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a concrete legislative defeat and the stated investor concerns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's policy push, though legislative defeat also reflects opposition strength and coalition limits.
contrary_evidence: Defeat in Congress is not the same as administrative incompetence, but it does show failure to convert the proposal into law.

evidence.claim: The OECD said uncertainty rose after electricity-market reform proposals, investment had been weak since 2015, and investors needed certainty about contracts and regulatory stability to restart growth.
evidence.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Mexico 2022
evidence.excerpt: The OECD said uncertainty rose after electricity-market reform proposals, investment had been weak since 2015, and investors needed certainty about contracts and regulatory stability to restart growth.
evidence.source_locator: summary text near the discussion of investment and electricity reform
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent economic survey with direct policy diagnosis and investment assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the 2022 policy environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's policy program and the uncertainty it created, though some investment weakness predates his term.
contrary_evidence: The OECD also acknowledged Mexico's solid macro framework, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a US$700 million operation tied to policies that simplify the business environment, promote financial inclusion, strengthen sustainable economic management, and help vulnerable groups benefit from growth.
evidence.title: Banco Mundial y México colaboran para impulsar el crecimiento económico inclusivo y sostenible
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a US$700 million operation tied to policies that simplify the business environment, promote financial inclusion, strengthen sustainable economic management, and help vulnerable groups benefit from growth.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and quoted remarks from the World Bank director
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent development-finance approval with explicit policy linkages and targeted objectives.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's policy agenda as adopted by the government, though the operation is a partnership and not a ruler-only achievement.
contrary_evidence: The approval confirms a policy framework, not final results.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Mexico's anti-inflation subsidies cost about 575 billion pesos in 2022, mostly through gasoline support, and officials said inflation would have been 2.6 percentage points higher without them.
evidence.title: Mexico anti-inflation subsidies come with $28 billion price tag
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Mexico's anti-inflation subsidies cost about 575 billion pesos in 2022, mostly through gasoline support, and officials said inflation would have been 2.6 percentage points higher without them.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with concrete fiscal and inflation claims; the exact counterfactual estimate is official and should be treated cautiously.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to AMLO's crisis-management strategy, though the inflation environment was also driven by global shocks.
contrary_evidence: Heavy subsidies have fiscal costs and do not demonstrate durable price control by themselves.

evidence.claim: ASF reported nine irregularities in the AIFA construction audits, including payments without documentation, uncredited materials, missing project and budget documentation, and other execution gaps across a 17,006 million peso sample.
evidence.title: Conoce las observaciones que la ASF hizo al AIFA
evidence.excerpt: ASF reported nine irregularities in the AIFA construction audits, including payments without documentation, uncredited materials, missing project and budget documentation, and other execution gaps across a 17,006 million peso sample.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Secondary reporting that directly quotes and summarizes the ASF's audit findings with concrete numeric detail.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to construction executed under AMLO's program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's flagship project implementation through the federal security/transport apparatus, though the audit concerns construction management rather than personal conduct.
contrary_evidence: Audit observations are not final judicial findings and may be partially clarified later.

evidence.claim: Pemex requested almost $6.5 billion more for Dos Bocas, pushing the refinery's projected cost to $14.6 billion, far above the original $8.9 billion budget, because of works not initially included and higher construction/startup costs.
evidence.title: Mexico's Pemex requests $6.5 billion more funding for 'Dos Bocas' refinery -documents, source
evidence.excerpt: Pemex requested almost $6.5 billion more for Dos Bocas, pushing the refinery's projected cost to $14.6 billion, far above the original $8.9 billion budget, because of works not initially included and higher construction/startup costs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting based on a document and multiple sources, with specific figures and budget comparisons.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's signature energy project and the administration's execution choices, though higher costs also reflect project complexity and inflation.
contrary_evidence: Cost escalation does not prove failure on its own; it does show serious budget pressure and incomplete initial planning.

evidence.claim: The ASF reported more than 573 million pesos in unresolved observations for La Escuela es Nuestra, including missing documentation, lack of proof of use of support funds, and the absence of periodic monitoring, supervision, and evaluation mechanisms.
evidence.title: La ASF detecta 573 mdp 'perdidos' en el programa La Escuela es Nuestra
evidence.excerpt: The ASF reported more than 573 million pesos in unresolved observations for La Escuela es Nuestra, including missing documentation, lack of proof of use of support funds, and the absence of periodic monitoring, supervision, and evaluation mechanisms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Secondary reporting that quotes and summarizes the ASF audit findings in detail, with specific amounts and mechanism failures.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, reviewing the program's 2020 operation and 2022 continuation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to AMLO's education policy design and rollout through SEP, though the audit concerns program controls rather than intent.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes that the predecessor schools-of-full-day model had positive learning findings, so the policy choice was a tradeoff rather than a blank failure.

evidence.claim: Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, used government-led Learning Camps to close foundational learning gaps, reaching thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and showing measurable gains in weeks.
evidence.title: Teaching at the Right Level supports learning recovery in Mexico
evidence.excerpt: Mexico's Ministry of Education, with UNICEF and partners, used government-led Learning Camps to close foundational learning gaps, reaching thousands of children with targeted literacy and numeracy instruction and showing measurable gains in weeks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF case study with concrete implementation and outcome language, albeit focused on a targeted intervention rather than the entire system.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to AMLO's education ministry and its recovery strategy, though UNICEF and partners share implementation and the case study is not a national average.
contrary_evidence: This is a case study of a targeted intervention, not a full audit of national learning outcomes.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Mexico's recovery accelerated in the first half of 2022 due to catch-up momentum, improving labor markets, and fiscal policy support, while weaker U.S. and global growth and tighter financial conditions were key drag factors; it also noted broadly neutral fiscal policy and untargeted subsidies to offset cost-of-living pressures.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with Mexico
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Mexico's recovery accelerated in the first half of 2022 due to catch-up momentum, improving labor markets, and fiscal policy support, while weaker U.S. and global growth and tighter financial conditions were key drag factors; it also noted broadly neutral fiscal policy and untargeted subsidies to offset cost-of-living pressures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Article IV surveillance with explicit macro attribution, policy description, and contemporaneous assessment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly attributable to AMLO's administration in combination with external shocks and inherited macro frameworks; the IMF explicitly separates policy support from external drag.
contrary_evidence: The IMF does not isolate AMLO-only causal shares, and some recovery drivers were inherited or external.

evidence.claim: The IMF said Mexico qualified for the Flexible Credit Line because of very strong macroeconomic policies and institutional policy frameworks, while also warning that a more turbulent external environment and rising external risks were complicating the recovery.
evidence.title: Mexico: Review Under the Flexible Credit Line Arrangement-Press Release; and Staff Report
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Mexico qualified for the Flexible Credit Line because of very strong macroeconomic policies and institutional policy frameworks, while also warning that a more turbulent external environment and rising external risks were complicating the recovery.
evidence.source_locator: summary/abstract and opening context in the IMF review
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent IMF review that explicitly links resilience to policy frameworks and notes external-risk pressure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This mostly reflects Mexico's institutional macro framework, some of which predated AMLO; the review is useful mainly for separating inherited resilience from AMLO-era policy choices.
contrary_evidence: Because the framework predates AMLO in part, this source limits how much credit can be assigned to 2022 ruler choices alone.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The Bienpesca and direct-benefit rollout shows concrete welfare distribution under AMLO's administration.
La Escuela es Nuestra shows a distinctive implementation model with direct local control over funds.
AIFA opening on time and within budget is a clear flagship infrastructure delivery claim.
The World Bank operation links AMLO's policy framework to inclusive and sustainable growth measures.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: ASF irregularities in AIFA construction show execution weaknesses and documentation problems.
ASF findings on La Escuela es Nuestra show monitoring and documentation gaps.
The electricity-overhaul defeat shows important policy failure at the legislative stage.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: AMLO inherited a state with deep inequality, weak growth, and entrenched energy and administrative constraints. The dossier shows large-scale social spending and some delivery, but also significant implementation problems and legislative resistance in key sectors.
judge.ruler_attribution: Strong on policy ownership and public-program direction, but mixed on implementation quality because some major projects and reforms faced audit findings, cost overruns, or congressional defeat. Attribution is good, but not clean across the whole portfolio.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Construction audit problems weaken the case for clean delivery.
Program controls and monitoring were inadequate in at least one major education initiative.
Legislative defeat reveals the administration could not always convert preference into law.

judge.source_mix: Official Mexican federal documents and portals, World Bank/UNICEF/IMF evidence, plus some Reuters and audit reporting. The evidence is broad and concrete, though some major items remain plan-heavy or audit-revealed failures.
judge.structured_prior_summary: No structured local priors were collected. The dossier is sufficiently rich to support a moderately strong but clearly mixed score.
judge.chapter_rationale: AMLO's 2022 record shows a real governing program and substantial state action, especially in social policy, education delivery, and flagship infrastructure. The administration could allocate resources, launch programs, and open major projects on schedule. But the same dossier also contains hard evidence of execution weaknesses, audit irregularities, and legislative defeat on a major policy push. That mix supports a middling-to-good score: capable in moving the state, but not consistently clean or fully effective in implementation.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the substantial direct-benefit delivery, budget priorities, and flagship project execution in the dossier.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score is not justified because the dossier also documents serious audit issues, policy defeats, and incomplete outcome verification.

chapter_specific.value: The score reflects administrative execution and program advancement, not moral approval of the program.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Andrés Manuel López Obrador's record on effectiveness in 2022 was assessed as generally positive, with important limitations, resulting in a score of 6.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The federal government issued a mandatory Program Estratégico de Salud para el Bienestar that aims to guarantee progressive, free, integral health services for people without social security and to strengthen federalization of health services; and La Escuela es Nuestra delivered funds directly to school parent committees, which decide use for construction, maintenance, equipment, longer hours, or student feeding.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: ASF reported nine irregularities in the AIFA construction audits, including payments without documentation, uncredited materials, missing project and budget documentation, and other execution gaps across a 17,006 million peso sample; and The ASF reported more than 573 million pesos in unresolved observations for La Escuela es Nuestra, including missing documentation, lack of proof of use of support funds, and the absence of periodic monitoring, supervision, and evaluation mechanisms.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Strong on policy ownership and public-program direction, but mixed on implementation quality because some major projects and reforms faced audit findings, cost overruns, or congressional defeat. Attribution is good, but not clean across the whole portfolio.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score is not justified because the dossier also documents serious audit issues, policy defeats, and incomplete outcome verification. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the substantial direct-benefit delivery, budget priorities, and flagship project execution in the dossier.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The government declared an indefinite humanitarian truce to save lives and facilitate aid delivery.
The UN welcomed the truce and urged a long-term ceasefire, confirming this was a real de-escalation step.
The later permanent cessation of hostilities agreement and Abiy's commitment to implementation were the year's strongest peace pivot.
UN humanitarian partners reported federal approval of resumed flights and operations, showing improved access after the peace pivot.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: UN experts found reasonable grounds to believe the federal government and allies committed crimes against humanity and used starvation as a method of warfare.
The HRW/Amnesty report tied serious abuses in Western Tigray to acquiescence and possible federal participation.
The UN Secretary-General said the situation was spiraling out of control and civilians were paying a horrific price.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Abiy inherited a severe internal war rather than an external interstate conflict, so the relevant question is whether he reduced violence and restored lawful order within that crisis.
judge.ruler_attribution: Attribution is mixed because many harms were carried out by federal allies or regional forces, but the truce, peace agreement, and implementation steps were still under Abiy's government authority.

contrary_evidence.explanation: Atrocity findings in the same year sharply limit any claim of a clean peace record.
The UN's 'no military solution' warning shows the conflict was still highly dangerous and unresolved.

judge.source_mix: UN, AU, humanitarian, and local reporting are combined with some official Ethiopian statements; local priors were unavailable in this experiment.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment; the judgment uses the embedded dossier, especially the late-year peace pivot and the contrary atrocity record.
judge.chapter_rationale: Abiy Ahmed's 2022 international-security record is mixed in a serious way. The year began with a humanitarian truce and ended with a cessation-of-hostilities agreement plus better humanitarian access, which are real peace achievements, but they sit beside grave atrocity allegations, starvation allegations, and a conflict environment that remained catastrophic for much of the year. The score therefore sits below the positive range, reflecting meaningful late-year restraint but not enough to overcome the severity of the year's violence.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A score of 3.5 is too low because the dossier includes genuine ceasefire, peace agreement, and access-improvement evidence.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A score of 5.5 is too high because the atrocities and civilian-harm findings remain severe and substantially undermine a restraint reading.

chapter_specific.value: From truce to peace agreement, but against a backdrop of grave civilian harm and disputed federal responsibility.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Abiy Ahmed's record on international peace in 2022 was assessed as mixed, resulting in a score of 4.5 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The government declared an indefinite humanitarian truce to save lives and facilitate aid delivery; and The Secretary-General welcomed Ethiopia's indefinite humanitarian truce and called for restoration of public services in Tigray, including banking, electricity, and telecommunications, and for a long-term ceasefire.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: The UN experts said there were reasonable grounds to believe the federal government and allies had committed crimes against humanity in Tigray and used starvation as a method of warfare; they also noted fighting had resumed after a five-month cessation of hostilities; and The report says Amhara regional security forces and civilian authorities in Western Tigray committed widespread abuses against Tigrayans with the acquiescence and possible participation of Ethiopian federal forces, including unlawful killings, sexual violence, detention, pillage, forcible transfer, and denial of humanitarian assistance.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Attribution is mixed because many harms were carried out by federal allies or regional forces, but the truce, peace agreement, and implementation steps were still under Abiy's government authority.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a score of 5.5 is too high because the atrocities and civilian-harm findings remain severe and substantially undermine a restraint reading. I did not go lower because a score of 3.5 is too low because the dossier includes genuine ceasefire, peace agreement, and access-improvement evidence.

evidence.claim: The Government of Ethiopia declared an indefinite humanitarian truce effective immediately on 24 March 2022 to save lives, reduce human suffering, and facilitate aid delivery to Tigray.
evidence.title: Gov't Declares Indefinite Humanitarian Truce
evidence.excerpt: The Government of Ethiopia declared an indefinite humanitarian truce effective immediately on 24 March 2022 to save lives, reduce human suffering, and facilitate aid delivery to Tigray.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statement with a precise date, purpose, and policy content.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period and central to the year's risk-de-escalation record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is a ruler-attributed government decision under Abiy Ahmed's premiership, though it is still conventional-conflict rather than nuclear policy.
contrary_evidence: The statement conditioned success on reciprocity from the other side.
Fighting later resumed, so the truce was not self-executing or durable on its own.

evidence.claim: Abiy said releasing some prisoners was meant to promote national unity, sustainable peace, and a better political environment for an inclusive national dialogue.
evidence.title: PM Abiy Says Government’s Decision to Release Prisoners Aims at Ensuring National Unity, Peace
evidence.excerpt: Abiy said releasing some prisoners was meant to promote national unity, sustainable peace, and a better political environment for an inclusive national dialogue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct state outlet report quoting Abiy on a dated domestic policy decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributed to Abiy Ahmed as PM, though it is a self-justifying official statement rather than independent verification of impact.
contrary_evidence: The same report also pairs the releases with a military ceremony and renewed hardline rhetoric toward the TPLF.
It does not prove the releases were broad, durable, or matched by full due-process reform.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Ethiopia freed Jawar Mohammed and Bekele Garba, granting them amnesty along with several other political activists arrested in 2020.
evidence.title: Ethiopia frees more top opposition leaders from prison
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Ethiopia freed Jawar Mohammed and Bekele Garba, granting them amnesty along with several other political activists arrested in 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire report with a concrete, dated domestic-release claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State action under Abiy Ahmed’s government; it supports restraint, but not a general claim of open civic space.
contrary_evidence: The release was limited to named figures and did not end broader detention practices.
The same period still saw conflict and security crackdowns elsewhere in the country.

evidence.claim: CPJ said Ethiopian authorities arrested at least 11 journalists and media workers since May 19 in Amhara and Addis Ababa as part of a broader crackdown that had already led to over 4,500 arrests.
evidence.title: Ethiopian authorities arrest 11 employees of 4 independent media outlets
evidence.excerpt: CPJ said Ethiopian authorities arrested at least 11 journalists and media workers since May 19 in Amhara and Addis Ababa as part of a broader crackdown that had already led to over 4,500 arrests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: CPJ is a specialized press-freedom monitor and the article gives names, dates, and detention circumstances.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The arrests are attributable to Ethiopian authorities under Abiy Ahmed’s government, though several were carried out by regional police forces.
contrary_evidence: Some detentions were justified by authorities as law-enforcement or anti-incitement actions.
The source does not itself establish a court finding of illegality for every arrest.

evidence.claim: Amnesty and HRW said Tigrayans in Western Tigray faced a campaign of killings, rape, mass detentions, and forcible transfers amounting to war crimes and crimes against humanity, with acquiescence and possible participation of Ethiopian federal forces.
evidence.title: Ethiopia: Crimes Against Humanity in Western Tigray Zone
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty and HRW said Tigrayans in Western Tigray faced a campaign of killings, rape, mass detentions, and forcible transfers amounting to war crimes and crimes against humanity, with acquiescence and possible participation of Ethiopian federal forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed joint rights report with explicit responsibility language and concrete abuse categories.
evidence.period_fit: In-period evidence that remained live in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report does not claim Abiy personally ordered every act, but it does tie the abuses to federal forces and the national government’s failure to stop them.
contrary_evidence: The federal and Amhara authorities denied ethnic cleansing allegations.
Some abuses were carried out by regional forces and militias rather than directly by the federal executive.

evidence.claim: HRW said Ethiopian authorities arbitrarily detained, mistreated, and forcibly disappeared thousands of ethnic Tigrayans deported from Saudi Arabia and transferred some to detention facilities in Afar and southern Ethiopia.
evidence.title: Ethiopia: Returned Tigrayans Detained, Abused
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Ethiopian authorities arbitrarily detained, mistreated, and forcibly disappeared thousands of ethnic Tigrayans deported from Saudi Arabia and transferred some to detention facilities in Afar and southern Ethiopia.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: HRW report based on documented accounts of post-deportation detention and abuse.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and part of the year’s inherited detention pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is attributable to Ethiopian authorities under Abiy Ahmed’s government, though the immediate trigger was Saudi deportations and wartime ethnicity profiling.
contrary_evidence: Saudi deportation policy is part of the causal chain, so Ethiopia is not the sole actor.
The source describes detention and abuse allegations, not a court judgment.

evidence.claim: HRW said journalists, civil society organizations, and outspoken public figures faced a hostile environment, and that government accountability efforts for abuses were inadequate and lacked transparency and independent oversight.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Ethiopia
evidence.excerpt: HRW said journalists, civil society organizations, and outspoken public figures faced a hostile environment, and that government accountability efforts for abuses were inadequate and lacked transparency and independent oversight.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country chapter from a major rights monitor, summarizing 2022 conditions with specific incidents and pattern claims.
evidence.period_fit: Covers 2022 directly, even though the page was published in 2023.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The report concerns national authorities under Abiy Ahmed and the security environment they controlled, but it still mixes federal, regional, and armed-group conduct.
contrary_evidence: The chapter also notes some de-escalatory steps, including the February emergency lift and the November cessation-of-hostilities agreement.
Because it is an annual summary, it compresses many incidents into a single narrative.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression.
evidence.title: Amnesty International Report 2022/23; The State of the World's Human Rights; Ethiopia 2022
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: ecoi.net is a secondary host, but the text is Amnesty’s country-report summary and is internally specific about 2022 conduct.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 with a concise year-end synthesis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is attributable to Abiy Ahmed’s federal government, though some conduct was implemented by security forces and regional actors.
contrary_evidence: The same source also notes the March humanitarian truce and partial resumption after the November agreement.
Some abuse was committed by Tigrayan forces in Afar, so not all violence is federal-side.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: Western Tigray abuses with acquiescence and possible participation of federal forces are among the strongest adverse facts.
Tigrayan deportees were arbitrarily detained and abused, showing persistent ethnic profiling and security failure.
The hostile environment for journalists and civil society, plus weak accountability, shows broader repression.
The federal government restricted aid to Tigray and held thousands arbitrarily detained, while accountability remained weak.
The large-scale crackdown in Amhara and journalist arrests show recurring coercive state behavior.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: The humanitarian truce is a real de-escalatory step and lowers the score from a more severe band.
Some prisoner releases and a dialogue-oriented framing show restraint and political opening at least in part.
UNHCR cooperation on refugee protection is a narrow positive protection signal.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: The year sits inside a war-and-postwar security crisis with fragmented federal, regional, and armed-group responsibility; the score reflects Abiy's responsibility for restraint, detention policy, and accountability rather than every local violent episode.
judge.ruler_attribution: Mixed and partly indirect: some harms are federal and some are regional or armed-group driven, but Abiy still governs the system and its response choices.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The humanitarian truce matters as restraint, even though it was not durable by itself.
Prisoner releases are a real restraint signal.
UNHCR cooperation on refugees shows some protective action.

judge.source_mix: Official statements, UN/IGO reporting, and rights NGOs; no client matrix used.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were unavailable across the lens set, so the judgment is based on the cited evidence and the embedded contrary notes.
judge.chapter_rationale: Abiy Ahmed's 2022 score is low because the year contains real state-related abuse, ethnic profiling, arbitrary detention, aid restrictions, and a weak accountability record. The affirmative evidence is not absent, but it is limited: a humanitarian truce, some prisoner releases, and a few protection-oriented actions. Those steps keep the score from falling into the deepest repression band, yet they do not overcome the large body of evidence on detention, censorship, and the federal government's failure to stop abuses. The right way to read the record is as a conflict-state with some restraint moves, not as a safely protective domestic order.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: I rejected 1-2 because the dossier shows severe coercion, but not the mass-terror floor for the bottom anchor.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: I rejected 4+ because the truce and releases are real but too partial to offset the broad coercive record and weak remedy.

chapter_specific.value: weak; some releases and truce steps, but limited durable remedy
constrained, especially around conflict and dissent
some de-escalation, but not enough to convert the year into a protective one
moderate to high system-level attribution, but with significant regional and armed-group complicating factors
3B.3 and 3B.7 are weaker than the detention, aid, and accountability lenses

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Abiy Ahmed's record on domestic safety in 2022 was assessed as poor, resulting in a score of 3 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: Amnesty and HRW said Tigrayans in Western Tigray faced a campaign of killings, rape, mass detentions, and forcible transfers amounting to war crimes and crimes against humanity, with acquiescence and possible participation of Ethiopian federal forces; and HRW said Ethiopian authorities arbitrarily detained, mistreated, and forcibly disappeared thousands of ethnic Tigrayans deported from Saudi Arabia and transferred some to detention facilities in Afar and southern Ethiopia.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: The Government of Ethiopia declared an indefinite humanitarian truce effective immediately on 24 March 2022 to save lives, reduce human suffering, and facilitate aid delivery to Tigray; and Abiy said releasing some prisoners was meant to promote national unity, sustainable peace, and a better political environment for an inclusive national dialogue.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed and partly indirect: some harms are federal and some are regional or armed-group driven, but Abiy still governs the system and its response choices.

Taken together, I did not go higher because I rejected 4+ because the truce and releases are real but too partial to offset the broad coercive record and weak remedy. I did not go lower because I rejected 1-2 because the dossier shows severe coercion, but not the mass-terror floor for the bottom anchor.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression.
evidence.title: Amnesty International Report 2022/23; The State of the World's Human Rights; Ethiopia 2022
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: ecoi.net is a secondary host, but the text is Amnesty’s country-report summary and is internally specific about 2022 conduct.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 with a concise year-end synthesis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is attributable to Abiy Ahmed’s federal government, though some conduct was implemented by security forces and regional actors.
contrary_evidence: The same source also notes the March humanitarian truce and partial resumption after the November agreement.
Some abuse was committed by Tigrayan forces in Afar, so not all violence is federal-side.

evidence.claim: Security personnel blocked 35 local civil society organizations from meeting the press in Addis Ababa to issue a joint peace statement.
evidence.title: News: Despite ban on meeting press, local CSOs call for immediate peace in Ethiopia, basic services provision in Tigray, other conflict hit areas
evidence.excerpt: Security personnel blocked 35 local civil society organizations from meeting the press in Addis Ababa to issue a joint peace statement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local reporting with a specific date, place, and event details; not official, but concrete and contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within September 2022 and squarely on target-year civic-space behavior.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The obstruction was carried out by security personnel who said they were from the government; attribution to Abiy is indirect through federal security control and the political context, not a documented personal order.
contrary_evidence: The CSOs still managed to publish the statement online after the blocked press event.
The government could frame the interference as a wartime security measure.

evidence.claim: Ethiopian authorities revoked Tom Gardner's press accreditation on May 13 and forced him to leave the country.
evidence.title: Ethiopia expels Economist correspondent Tom Gardner
evidence.excerpt: Ethiopian authorities revoked Tom Gardner's press accreditation on May 13 and forced him to leave the country.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist press-freedom monitor; the event is dated, specific, and corroborated by the outlet and regulator.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about press access under the Abiy government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The action was taken by the Ethiopian Media Authority, a statutory regulator operating under the state; attribution to Abiy is strongest as a government-pattern action, not a personally documented order.
contrary_evidence: The authority said Gardner had failed professional standards and was willing to license another correspondent.
The government could frame the move as a regulatory, not political, decision.

evidence.claim: As of November 4, 2022, authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years.
evidence.title: Two years of internet shutdowns: people in Tigray, Ethiopia, deserve better
evidence.excerpt: As of November 4, 2022, authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Leading shutdown monitor with a precise, time-stamped, region-specific claim.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within target-year 2022 and describing an ongoing restriction that remained in force during most of the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The shutdown is attributed to Ethiopian authorities; the evidence does not identify Abiy personally ordering it, but it is a federal policy choice within his government's authority.
contrary_evidence: Government officials have cited war-time disinformation and security concerns as justification for the blackout.
The article notes peace talks and calls for restoring access, so the network closure was contested.

evidence.claim: The national dialogue excluded key rebel groups, and opposition figures accused the government of trying to orchestrate the process and control who participated.
evidence.title: Ethiopia launches a national dialogue, but divisions run deep
evidence.excerpt: The national dialogue excluded key rebel groups, and opposition figures accused the government of trying to orchestrate the process and control who participated.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Field reporting with named interlocutors, concrete dates, and direct quotations from critics and the commission.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 with retrospective context from late 2021 on commission formation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The article attributes the process to Abiy's government and his public push for the dialogue, but also records that the commission claimed independence; attribution is mixed and not equivalent to a proven personal directive.
contrary_evidence: The commission and government argued the dialogue was inclusive and open to peaceful participants.
The report also notes some observers saw the process as potentially useful if managed properly.

evidence.claim: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration.
evidence.title: National Dialogue Commission, Civil Society Organizations Council Ink Partnership Agreement
evidence.excerpt: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official contemporaneous report on a formal government-supported institutional step; credible for the existence of the agreement, less so for its effectiveness.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly about political-process institutions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects a state-backed institutional initiative under Abiy's government; it is strong for formal commitment, weaker for proving independent operation or actual openness.
contrary_evidence: The agreement does not show that the dialogue was truly independent or inclusive in practice.
Earlier and later reporting still described exclusion and control concerns.

evidence.claim: Freedom House said Article 93 allows suspension of political and democratic rights during a state of emergency, and that authorities used emergency powers in late 2021 and early 2022 to crack down on media houses and arrest online and broadcast journalists.
evidence.title: Ethiopia: Freedom on the Net 2022 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: Freedom House said Article 93 allows suspension of political and democratic rights during a state of emergency, and that authorities used emergency powers in late 2021 and early 2022 to crack down on media houses and arrest online and broadcast journalists.
evidence.source_locator: country report text around Article 93 and the state-of-emergency discussion
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Established rights monitor with direct country-report analysis and specific legal-context claims.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the 2022 period and the emergency powers still affecting the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to federal authorities under Abiy's government; the report separates legal basis from the implementation of restrictions, but not every action is individually ordered by him in the text.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that the six-month state of emergency was lifted in February 2022, so some restrictions were inherited from the prior emergency period.

evidence.claim: Access Now said authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years, preventing communication, access to information, and accountability over violence.
evidence.title: Two years of internet shutdowns: people in Tigray, Ethiopia, deserve better
evidence.excerpt: Access Now said authorities had kept Tigray under an internet shutdown for two years, preventing communication, access to information, and accountability over violence.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporaneous rights-monitor reporting on a specific shutdown and its political effects.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and explicitly about the shutdown's duration up to that date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Ethiopian authorities; this supports the de facto command path even though the underlying written order is not exposed in the public source.
contrary_evidence: Access Now is an advocacy source, so it is strong on the existence and effect of the shutdown but weaker on the precise internal command chain.

decisive_positive_evidence.explanation: The National Dialogue Commission and civil-society partnership show a formal institutional attempt at political inclusion.
The blocked CSO press event still resulted in a published peace statement, which is a narrow sign that civic actors were not fully silenced.

decisive_negative_evidence.explanation: Amnesty says federal authorities restricted aid to Tigray, arbitrarily detained thousands, and eroded freedom of expression in 2022.
The expulsion of a correspondent shows direct press restriction by state authorities under the Abiy government.
The internet shutdown in Tigray remained in force through most of 2022, severely restricting access and accountability.
Freedom House links emergency powers to crackdowns on media and journalists, confirming that restrictions were not isolated.
Access Now's two-year shutdown documentation underscores the breadth and duration of digital control.

judge.inherited_baseline_and_constraints: Ethiopia in 2022 was shaped by war, emergency powers, and severe security pressures. Abiy's government had some reformist and consultative language, but the practical environment remained coercive and information-restricted.
judge.ruler_attribution: Mixed but substantial: the evidence often attributes actions to federal security authorities and emergency powers under Abiy's government, even when it lacks a personal order transcript.

contrary_evidence.explanation: The National Dialogue Commission partnership is the main mitigating fact, but it does not overcome the coercive record.
The published peace statement shows partial civic space, not durable freedom.

judge.source_mix: Amnesty, Access Now, CPJ, Freedom House, and local reporting. The evidence is consistent on repression and digital controls, with formal dialogue efforts providing only limited counterweight.
judge.structured_prior_summary: Structured local priors were not collected in this experiment; the judge relied entirely on the embedded projection and its cited evidence.
judge.chapter_rationale: Abiy Ahmed's 2022 Ethiopia is significantly constrained and coercive, though not as sealed as the hardest authoritarian cases. The clearest negative facts are aid restrictions in Tigray, arrests and press expulsions, and a long-running shutdown that cut off communication and accountability. The dialogue commission and civil-society partnership are real but too thin to counterbalance the broader pattern of emergency rule and information control. The score therefore sits in the lower-middle range: serious political-freedom erosion, but still some formal institutional movement rather than total closure.
judge.lower_anchor_rejected: A lower score would ignore the partial consultative institutions and the fact that the system was coercive but not fully closed in the same way as the hardest authoritarian cases.
judge.higher_anchor_rejected: A higher score would overread the dialogue and partnership gestures. The operative reality was still detentions, shutdowns, and press restrictions under emergency powers.

chapter_specific.value: Erosive under emergency and conflict conditions: consultation existed on paper, but coercive control dominated practice.

judge.reader_abstract:
Overall, Abiy Ahmed's record on political freedom in 2022 was assessed as poor, resulting in a score of 3 out of 10.

Evidence supporting a more favorable assessment includes the following: The National Dialogue Commission signed a partnership agreement with the Ethiopian Civil Society Organizations Council to work in collaboration; and Security personnel blocked 35 local civil society organizations from meeting the press in Addis Ababa to issue a joint peace statement.

Evidence weighing against a stronger assessment includes the following: Amnesty said the federal government restricted aid to Tigray, halted deliveries from August to November, held thousands of Tigrayan detainees arbitrarily, failed to implement accountability, and significantly eroded freedom of expression; and Ethiopian authorities revoked Tom Gardner's press accreditation on May 13 and forced him to leave the country.

Responsibility and evidentiary limits matter here: Mixed but substantial: the evidence often attributes actions to federal security authorities and emergency powers under Abiy's government, even when it lacks a personal order transcript.

Taken together, I did not go higher because a higher score would overread the dialogue and partnership gestures. The operative reality was still detentions, shutdowns, and press restrictions under emergency powers. I did not go lower because a lower score would ignore the partial consultative institutions and the fact that the system was coercive but not fully closed in the same way as the hardest authoritarian cases.
